    # Inner-loop unrolling (micro-optimization)
    # ---------------------------------------
    # Unroll the innermost n-loop in the correlation kernel to reduce
    # loop-control overhead and expose more instruction-level parallelism.
    # This is particularly effective when combined with vectorization.
    unroll(n, 4)
--- END OF MODEL: correlation-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: correlation-02 ---
domain:
    # N: number of observations (rows)
    # M: number of variables/features (columns)
    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index for data
    j: dim in [0, M)        # column index for data
    k: dim in [0, N)        # reduction index over rows (for correlation)
    p: dim in [0, M)        # row index in correlation matrix
    q: dim in [0, M)        # column index in correlation matrix

data:
    # Row-major storage as in C: data[i][j] ~ base + (i * M + j)
    data[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j
        # Initially: raw input data
        # After normalization: centered & scaled data

    mean[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # Column means

    stddev[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # Column standard deviations (population, with epsilon clamp)

    inv_scale[j]: temp DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j]) – used to replace per-element divisions
        # Extra memory is O(M), << 50% of original footprint.

    corr[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q
        # M x M symmetric correlation matrix, row-major

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE        # = N, but passed as DATA_TYPE
    eps: DATA_TYPE            # = 0.1
    # Tuning parameters for blocking / vectorization:
    T_I_1: int > 0            # tile size for i in data sweeps
    T_J_1: int > 0            # tile size for j in data sweeps
    T_P:   int > 0            # tile size for p in corr
    T_Q:   int > 0            # tile size for q in corr
    T_K:   int > 0            # tile size for k reduction in corr
    VEC_WIDTH: int > 0        # SIMD width (elements per vector)
    UNROLL_K: int > 0         # unroll factor for k-loop in corr

computation:
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Compute column means: mean[j] = (1/float_n) * sum_i data[i,j]
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    MEAN_INIT:
      for j:
        mean[j] = 0.0

    # Reordered as i-outer, j-inner to traverse data row-major (contiguous j)
    # instead of the original j-outer, i-inner strided access.
    MEAN_ACCUM:
      for i:
        for j:
          mean[j] += data[i, j]

    MEAN_SCALE:
      for j:
        mean[j] = mean[j] / float_n

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Accumulate variances while centering data in-place
    #    stddev[j] accumulates sum_i (data_raw[i,j] - mean[j])^2
    #    data is updated to (data_raw[i,j] - mean[j])
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    STDDEV_INIT:
      for j:
        stddev[j] = 0.0

    # Combined centering and variance accumulation, still using row-major order.
    # Note: Implementation can use a scalar temporary to avoid recomputing
    #       (data[i,j] - mean[j]) twice; here we express semantics only.
    CENTER_AND_VAR:
      for i:
        for j:
          stddev[j] += (data[i, j] - mean[j]) * (data[i, j] - mean[j])
          data[i, j] = data[i, j] - mean[j]

    STDDEV_FINISH:
      for j:
        stddev[j] = stddev[j] / float_n       # variance
        stddev[j] = sqrt(stddev[j])           # standard deviation
        # Epsilon clamp to avoid division by (near-)zero in normalization
        stddev[j] = (stddev[j] <= eps) ? 1.0 : stddev[j]

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Precompute 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    #    This hoists sqrt(float_n) and divisions out of the N*M loops.
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    PREPARE_SCALE:
      sqrt_float_n = sqrt(float_n)
      for j:
        inv_scale[j] = 1.0 / (sqrt_float_n * stddev[j])

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Scale data in-place.
    #    After this: data[i,j] = (raw[i,j] - mean[j]) / (sqrt(float_n)*stddev[j])
    #    Each column has variance 1/float_n and sum_i data[i,j]^2 = 1.
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    SCALE_DATA:
      for i:
        for j:
          data[i, j] = data[i, j] * inv_scale[j]

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Compute symmetric correlation matrix:
    #    corr[p,q] = sum_k data[k,p]*data[k,q], with corr[p,p] = 1.
    #    This is C = Z^T * Z for Z = normalized data, but we exploit symmetry
    #    and write only upper triangle, mirroring to lower.
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    CORR_DIAGONAL:
      for p:
        corr[p, p] = 1.0

    CORR_OFFDIAGONAL:
      for p:
        for q:
          if p < q:
            corr[p, q] = sum(k, data[k, p] * data[k, q])
            corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]

dependencies:
    # Mean must be fully computed before any use of mean[j].
    for j in [0, M):
      MEAN_INIT(j) -> MEAN_ACCUM(i, j)
      MEAN_ACCUM(i, j) -> MEAN_SCALE(j)

    # Variance accumulation and centering depend on finalized mean.
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
      MEAN_SCALE(j) -> STDDEV_INIT(j)
      STDDEV_INIT(j) -> CENTER_AND_VAR(i, j)

    for j in [0, M):
      CENTER_AND_VAR(i, j) -> STDDEV_FINISH(j)

    # inv_scale[j] depends on finalized stddev[j] and float_n.
    for j in [0, M):
      STDDEV_FINISH(j) -> PREPARE_SCALE(j)

    # Scaling data depends on inv_scale[j] and centered data.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
      PREPARE_SCALE(j) -> SCALE_DATA(i, j)

    # Correlation uses fully normalized data.
    for p in [0, M), q in [0, M), k in [0, N):
      SCALE_DATA(k, p) -> CORR_OFFDIAGONAL(p, q)
      SCALE_DATA(k, q) -> CORR_OFFDIAGONAL(p, q)

optimization:
    #==========================================================
    # High-level goals:
    #  - Use row-major (i,j) traversal for good cache locality.
    #  - Avoid repeated expensive operations: sqrt(float_n), division.
    #  - Expose parallelism over independent columns/column-pairs.
    #  - Map correlation to a tiled symmetric matrix multiply (Z^T * Z).
    #==========================================================

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # A) Data sweeps (MEAN_ACCUM, CENTER_AND_VAR, SCALE_DATA)
    #    over (i,j) space
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Use 2D blocking to improve cache reuse on data[i,j] and mean/stddev.
    block(i, I1, T_I_1)          # tile rows of data
    block(j, J1, T_J_1)          # tile columns of data
    hoist(I1)                    # outermost tile over rows
    hoist(J1)                    # next tile over columns

    # Vectorize along j, the contiguous dimension in row-major layout.
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)

    # Parallelize row-tiles across cores. For MEAN_ACCUM and CENTER_AND_VAR,
    # this implies a reduction on mean[j] and stddev[j], respectively.
    # + Operations are associative/commutative enough for FP reductions.
    parallelize(I1)

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # B) Correlation phase: corr = data^T * data (symmetric GEMM)
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Treat CORR_OFFDIAGONAL as a symmetric matrix multiplication of the
    # normalized data matrix with its transpose, with domain p < q.
    # Use 3D tiling over (p,q,k) to improve locality in both data and corr.
    block(p, P, T_P)             # tile over first variable index
    block(q, Q, T_Q)             # tile over second variable index
    block(k, K, T_K)             # tile over observation/reduction dimension

    hoist(P)
    hoist(Q)
    hoist(K)

    # Parallelize tiles of (P,Q): each tile updates a disjoint submatrix of corr.
    # The triangular constraint p < q is enforced inside tiles, so no races.
    parallelize(P)
    # Optionally, a runtime could "collapse" (P,Q) to 2D-parallelize.
    # (Not explicitly modeled; left to the backend.)

    # Vectorize along k in the innermost reduction loop, which has unit-stride
    # accesses in the first dimension of data[k, p] and data[k, q].
    vectorize(k, VEC_WIDTH)

    # Unroll the k-loop to improve ILP and better hide memory latency.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # C) Strength reduction and hoisting
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Already modeled explicitly in the computation:
    #  - PREPARE_SCALE hoists sqrt(float_n) out of all inner loops.
    #  - inv_scale[j] replaces N*M per-element divisions with:
    #        M per-column divisions + N*M multiplications.
    # No additional directives needed; code generators should map
    # PREPARE_SCALE + SCALE_DATA to scalar precomputation + SIMD muls.
--- END OF MODEL: correlation-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: correlation-03 ---
domain:
    # N: number of rows / observations
    # M: number of columns / variables
    n:  dim in [0, N)
    c:  dim in [0, M)
    c1: dim in [0, M)
    c2: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # Row-major 2D input, updated in-place to hold normalized data
    data[n, c]: inout DATA_TYPE = (n, c) -> n * M + c

    # Row-major 2D output: correlation matrix (M x M)
    corr[c1, c2]: out DATA_TYPE = (c1, c2) -> c1 * M + c2

    # 1D temporaries / outputs for each column
    mean[c]:   out  DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c
    stddev[c]: out  DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c

    # Additional 1D temporary: scaling factor per column.
    # scale[c] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[c]).
    # This costs only O(M) extra memory (< 50% overhead of original footprint).
    scale[c]:  tmp  DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c

parameters:
    float_n: in DATA_TYPE          # = (DATA_TYPE) N
    eps:     in DATA_TYPE          # = SCALAR_VAL(0.1)

    # Tuning parameters for the target x64 machine (to be chosen empirically)
    VEC_M:   in int                # vector width along contiguous column dimension
    TC:      in int                # tile size in column dimensions (for corr)
    TN:      in int                # tile size in row dimension (for corr)
    UC1:     in int                # unroll factor for c1 loop in corr
    UN:      in int                # unroll factor for n loop in corr

computation:

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Column means
    #    mean[c] = (1/float_n) * sum_n data[n, c]
    #    Implemented with row-major traversal (n outer, c inner).
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    mean_stage_init:
        for c:
            mean[c] = (DATA_TYPE)0.0

    mean_stage_accumulate:
        for n:
            for c:
                mean[c] += data[n, c]

    mean_stage_finalize:
        for c:
            mean[c] /= float_n

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Column standard deviations and per-column scaling factors
    #
    #    var[c]    = (1/float_n) * sum_n (data[n, c] - mean[c])^2
    #    stddev[c] = sqrt(var[c])
    #    if stddev[c] <= eps: stddev[c] = 1.0   (avoid division by ~0)
    #
    #    Precompute:
    #      sqrt_n      = sqrt(float_n)
    #      inv_sqrt_n  = 1 / sqrt_n
    #      scale[c]    = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[c]
    #
    #    scale[c] is later used to normalize data with only multiplies.
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    stddev_stage_init:
        for c:
            stddev[c] = (DATA_TYPE)0.0

    # Local scalars (conceptually hoisted once)
    sqrt_n:      scalar DATA_TYPE
    inv_sqrt_n:  scalar DATA_TYPE

    compute_sqrt_n:
        sqrt_n     = SQRT_FUN(float_n)
        inv_sqrt_n = ((DATA_TYPE)1.0) / sqrt_n

    stddev_stage_accumulate:
        for n:
            for c:
                tmp = data[n, c] - mean[c]
                stddev[c] += tmp * tmp

    stddev_stage_finalize:
        for c:
            stddev[c] /= float_n
            stddev[c]  = SQRT_FUN(stddev[c])
            stddev[c]  = stddev[c] <= eps ? (DATA_TYPE)1.0 : stddev[c]

            # scale[c] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[c])
            scale[c]   = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[c]

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Center and normalize the data in-place
    #
    #    data[n, c] <- (data[n, c] - mean[c]) * scale[c]
    #
    #    This matches the original:
    #      data -= mean; data /= sqrt(float_n) * stddev
    #    but uses one subtraction and two multiplies instead of
    #    repeated sqrt and division.
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    normalize_stage:
        for n:
            for c:
                data[n, c] = (data[n, c] - mean[c]) * scale[c]

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Correlation matrix on normalized data
    #
    #    For i != j:
    #      corr[i, j] = sum_n data[n, i] * data[n, j]
    #      corr[j, i] = corr[i, j]
    #    And corr[i, i] = 1.0 exactly.
    #
    #    We compute only the upper triangle via a symmetric
    #    rank-k update with row-major friendly traversal.
    #------------------------------------------------------------------

    # 4a. Initialize upper triangle (including diagonal) to 0
    corr_init:
        for c1:
            for c2 in [c1, M):
                corr[c1, c2] = (DATA_TYPE)0.0

    # 4b. Accumulate dot products:
    #     for each row n, update all (c1, c2 >= c1) pairs using that row.
    #
    #     This touches data[n, *] in row-major order and corr[* , *]
    #     in mostly row-major order (c2 innermost).
    corr_accum:
        for n:
            for c1:
                v1 = data[n, c1]
                for c2 in [c1, M):
                    corr[c1, c2] += v1 * data[n, c2]

    # 4c. Enforce symmetry and set diagonal exactly to 1.0
    corr_sym:
        for c1:
            corr[c1, c1] = (DATA_TYPE)1.0
            for c2 in [c1 + 1, M):
                corr[c2, c1] = corr[c1, c2]

optimization:

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mean and stddev computation: improve locality and exploit parallelism
    #------------------------------------------------------------------

    # Means:
    #  - As written, mean_stage_accumulate already uses (n outer, c inner),
    #    which matches row-major layout of data.
    #  - Parallelize across rows with a reduction on mean[c].
    mean_stage_accumulate: parallelize(n)          # reduction into mean[c]
    mean_stage_accumulate: vectorize(c, VEC_M)     # SIMD over contiguous columns

    # Stddev + scale:
    #  - Same row-major traversal.
    #  - Parallelize across n with reduction into stddev[c].
    stddev_stage_accumulate: parallelize(n)        # reduction into stddev[c]
    stddev_stage_accumulate: vectorize(c, VEC_M)

    # Finalization over columns is small; can be vectorized.
    stddev_stage_finalize: vectorize(c, VEC_M)

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Normalization: fully element-wise and embarrassingly parallel
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    normalize_stage: parallelize(n)
    normalize_stage: vectorize(c, VEC_M)

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Correlation accumulation: main hotspot
    #
    # Treat corr_accum as a symmetric rank-k update:
    #   corr += data^T * data   (upper triangle only).
    #
    # Strategy:
    #   - Tile both column dimensions (c1, c2) and the row dimension n.
    #   - Assign tile pairs (C1b, C2b) with C2b >= C1b to threads
    #     (no write sharing between threads).
    #   - Within each tile, traverse data row-major and corr row-major.
    #------------------------------------------------------------------

    # Tile column and row dimensions
    corr_accum: block(c1, C1b, TC)    # outer column tiles
    corr_accum: block(c2, C2b, TC)    # inner column tiles
    corr_accum: block(n,  Nb, TN)     # row tiles

    # Hoist tile loops to outermost levels
    corr_accum: hoist(C1b)
    corr_accum: hoist(C2b)
    corr_accum: hoist(Nb)

    # Parallelize over 2D column tiles.
    # Implementation must restrict to C2b >= C1b so only upper-triangular
    # tile pairs are computed, preserving original flop count.
    corr_accum: parallelize(C1b, C2b)

    # Within each tile:
    #   for Nb (rows in tile)
    #     for c1 in C1b
    #       v1 = data[n, c1]
    #       for c2 in C2b ∩ [c1, M)
    #         corr[c1, c2] += v1 * data[n, c2]
    #
    # Keep c2 as the innermost loop for contiguous accesses to corr and data.
    corr_accum: interchange(n, c1)        # order: Nb -> c1 -> n -> c2 or Nb -> n -> c1 -> c2
    corr_accum: interchange(c1, c2)       # ensure c2 is innermost within tile

    # Vectorize over c2 (contiguous in memory) and unroll small loops.
    corr_accum: vectorize(c2, VEC_M)
    corr_accum: unroll(c1, UC1)
    corr_accum: unroll(n,  UN)

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Symmetrization and diagonal setup: cheap but parallelizable if desired
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    corr_sym: parallelize(c1)
    corr_sym: vectorize(c2, VEC_M)
--- END OF MODEL: correlation-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: correlation-04 ---
domain:
    # Problem sizes (fixed at runtime via N, M)
    r: dim in [0, N)          # sample index (row of data)
    c: dim in [0, M)          # feature index / column of data
    p: dim in [0, M)          # row index of correlation matrix (feature index)
    q: dim in [0, M)          # column index of correlation matrix (feature index)
    k: dim in [0, N)          # reduction index over samples for correlation

data:
    # Input data matrix: N samples × M features, row-major as in C
    data[r, c]: inout DATA_TYPE = (r, c) -> r * M + c

    # Output correlation matrix: M × M, row-major
    corr[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q

    # Column-wise statistics
    mean[c]: inout DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c        # column means
    stddev[c]: inout DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c      # column standard deviations

    # Additional temporary scaling factors (small, O(M) memory)
    norm_factor[c]: temp DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c
        # = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[c]) after stddev has been clamped

parameters:
    # Problem dimensions (known at compile-time via macros N, M, but modeled as parameters)
    N: int
    M: int

    # Scalar parameters from the C code
    float_n: DATA_TYPE        # equals (DATA_TYPE) N
    eps: DATA_TYPE            # = 0.1, near-zero stddev threshold

    # Pre-hoisted scalar factors (computed once)
    inv_float_n: DATA_TYPE    # = 1.0 / float_n
    sqrt_float_n: DATA_TYPE   # = sqrt(float_n)

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen for the target machine)
    TILE_R: int               # tile size along r (rows of data)
    TILE_C: int               # tile size along c (columns of data)
    TILE_P: int               # tile size along p (corr rows / features)
    TILE_Q: int               # tile size along q (corr cols / features)
    TILE_K: int               # tile size along k (samples in corr reduction)
    VEC_WIDTH: int            # SIMD width in elements along contiguous dimensions
    UNROLL_R: int             # unroll factor along r
    UNROLL_C: int             # unroll factor along c
    UNROLL_P: int             # unroll factor along p (corr feature index)

computation:
    # 1. Compute column means:
    #    mean[c] = (1/float_n) * sum_r data[r, c]
    MEAN:
      # Initialize means
      for c:
        mean[c] = 0

      # Accumulate sums over rows
      for r:
        for c:
          mean[c] += data[r, c]

      # Scale by 1 / float_n
      for c:
        mean[c] *= inv_float_n

    # 2. Compute column standard deviations with near-zero handling:
    #    sigma2[c] = (1/float_n) * sum_r (data[r, c] - mean[c])^2
    #    s = sqrt(sigma2[c])
    #    stddev[c] = (s <= eps ? 1.0 : s)
    STDDEV:
      # Initialize variances to zero
      for c:
        stddev[c] = 0

      # Accumulate squared deviations
      for r:
        for c:
          let diff = data[r, c] - mean[c] in
            stddev[c] += diff * diff

      # Finalize stddev: divide by N, sqrt, and clamp to avoid division by near-zero
      for c:
        stddev[c] *= inv_float_n
        stddev[c] = sqrt(stddev[c])
        stddev[c] = (stddev[c] <= eps ? SCALAR_VAL(1.0) : stddev[c])

    # 3. Precompute normalized scaling factors per column:
    #    norm_factor[c] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[c])
    # This replaces a division per element in the normalization step with
    # a multiplication by a precomputed factor.
    NORM_FACTOR:
      for c:
        norm_factor[c] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (sqrt_float_n * stddev[c])

    # 4. Center and reduce (normalize) the columns in-place:
    #    data[r, c] := (data[r, c] - mean[c]) * norm_factor[c]
    #
    # After this step, each column has zero mean and unit L2 norm, so that
    #   corr[p, q] = sum_r data[r, p] * data[r, q]
    # computes the correlation coefficients directly, and diag(corr) = 1.
    NORMALIZE:
      for r:
        for c:
          let centered = data[r, c] - mean[c] in
            data[r, c] = centered * norm_factor[c]

    # 5. Compute the m × m correlation matrix.
    #
    # Semantics (matching the original C kernel):
    #   - corr[p, p] = 1 for all p
    #   - for p < q:
    #         corr[p, q] = sum_r data[r, p] * data[r, q]
    #         corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]
    #
    # We express this as an upper-triangular reduction and an explicit
    # symmetrization step.
    CORR_UPPER:
      # Initialize upper triangle (including diagonal) to 0;
      # diagonal will be overwritten with 1 later.
      for p in [0, M):
        for q in [p, M):
          corr[p, q] = 0

      # Accumulate correlation via a symmetric rank‑k update:
      # rearranged loop order compared to the C code for better row reuse
      for k:
        for p in [0, M):
          let x = data[k, p] in
            for q in [p, M):
              corr[p, q] += x * data[k, q]

    CORR_SYMM:
      # Set diagonal to exactly 1 and copy upper triangle to lower triangle
      for p in [0, M):
        corr[p, p] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)
        for q in [p + 1, M):
          corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]

dependencies:
    # High-level phase ordering (implied by data flow, made explicit here):
    for c in [0, M):
      MEAN -> STDDEV
      STDDEV -> NORM_FACTOR
      NORM_FACTOR -> NORMALIZE

    for p in [0, M), q in [p, M):
      NORMALIZE -> CORR_UPPER
      CORR_UPPER -> CORR_SYMM

optimization:
    # -------------------------------
    # General scalar hoisting
    # -------------------------------
    # Compute inv_float_n and sqrt_float_n once before all loops.
    # This removes repeated divisions and sqrt calls inside hot loops.
    hoist(inv_float_n)          # inv_float_n = 1.0 / float_n
    hoist(sqrt_float_n)         # sqrt_float_n = sqrt(float_n)

    # -------------------------------
    # Mean and stddev computation
    # -------------------------------
    # Accesses to data[r, c] are row-major contiguous in c,
    # so we tile and vectorize along c, and parallelize over tiles of r.
    block(r, R, TILE_R)
    block(c, C, TILE_C)

    # Within tiled loops:
    #   for R in ...
    #     parallel for r in R      # rows split across threads
    #       vectorized for c in C  # contiguous columns
    parallelize(R)
    vectorize(C, VEC_WIDTH)
    unroll(C, UNROLL_C)

    # Apply the same tiling and parallelization to STDDEV and NORMALIZE,
    # since they have the same iteration structure over (r, c).
    apply_to(STDDEV, NORMALIZE):
        block(r, R, TILE_R)
        block(c, C, TILE_C)
        parallelize(R)
        vectorize(C, VEC_WIDTH)
        unroll(C, UNROLL_C)

    # -------------------------------
    # Correlation accumulation (CORR_UPPER)
    # -------------------------------
    # Treat corr = data^T * data as a symmetric rank‑k update, but only
    # compute the upper triangle (p <= q). Use 3D blocking for better
    # cache reuse over data and corr, and to expose parallelism.
    block(k, K, TILE_K)         # tiles along the samples dimension
    block(p, P, TILE_P)         # tiles along correlation row (feature) index
    block(q, Q, TILE_Q)         # tiles along correlation col (feature) index

    # Order tiles as:
    #   for K:
    #     for P:
    #       for Q starting at P (only upper-triangular tiles):
    #         for k in K, p in P, q in [max(p, Q_start), Q_end):
    hoist(K)
    hoist(P)
    hoist(Q)

    # Parallelize over tiles of P (and/or Q) since each (p, q) in the upper
    # triangle is updated independently in the k-reduction.
    parallelize(P)

    # Within each tile, make q the innermost loop to benefit from contiguous
    # access to data[k, q] and corr[p, q].
    vectorize(q, VEC_WIDTH)
    unroll(p, UNROLL_P)

    # Optionally use a small on-chip temporary tile buffer corr_block[P, Q]
    # for each (P, Q) tile:
    #   - initialize corr_block to 0
    #   - accumulate over k in K into corr_block
    #   - write corr_block back to corr at the end of the (P, Q, K) tile
    # This buffer is of size TILE_P * TILE_Q and can be chosen so that
    #   TILE_P * TILE_Q * sizeof(DATA_TYPE)
    # stays well below 50% of the original total memory footprint.

    # -------------------------------
    # Correlation symmetrization (CORR_SYMM)
    # -------------------------------
    # The symmetrization step writes corr[q, p] = corr[p, q] for p < q
    # and sets corr[p, p] = 1. Each (p, q) pair is independent, so we
    # parallelize over p and vectorize over q.
    parallelize(p)
    vectorize(q, VEC_WIDTH)
    unroll(p, UNROLL_P)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)          # observation index (rows of data)
    j: dim in [0, M)          # variable index (columns of data)
    p: dim in [0, M)          # row index of correlation matrix
    q: dim in [0, M)          # column index of correlation matrix
    k: dim in [0, N)          # reduction index over observations

data:
    # Store data column-major so that scans over i/k are contiguous in memory.
    # This matches all heavy inner loops (means, stddev, normalization, correlation),
    # which iterate over observations for a fixed column/variable.
    data[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> j * N + i
        # Column-major: each column j is stored as a contiguous N-element vector

    mean[j]:   inout DATA_TYPE = j -> j        # per-variable mean
    stddev[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = j -> j        # per-variable stddev (after epsilon clamp)

    corr[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q
        # Row-major correlation matrix, as in the original C code

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE    # N as a floating-point value
    eps: DATA_TYPE        # small epsilon avoiding division by tiny stddevs

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    Ti: int               # tile size in observation dimension (i, k) for all reductions
    Tj: int               # tile size in variable / correlation dimensions (j, p, q)
    Tk: int               # tile size in reduction dimension k for correlation
    VF: int               # vector width for innermost loops (e.g., 4 or 8 for x86_64)

computation:
    # Hoist scalar computations that are invariant across all loops.
    PRECOMPUTE:
        inv_n      = 1.0 / float_n              # used in mean and variance
        sqrt_n     = sqrt(float_n)              # SQRT_FUN(float_n) in original code
        inv_sqrt_n = 1.0 / sqrt_n               # used in normalization

    # 1. Compute column means: mean[j] = (1/N) * sum_i data[i,j]
    MEAN:
        for j:
            mean[j] = inv_n * sum(i, data[i, j])

    # 2. Compute standard deviations (with epsilon guard):
    #    stddev[j] = sqrt( (1/N) * sum_i (data[i,j] - mean[j])^2 )
    #    if stddev[j] <= eps then stddev[j] = 1.0
    STDDEV:
        for j:
            tmp = sum(i, (data[i, j] - mean[j]) * (data[i, j] - mean[j]))
            tmp = inv_n * tmp
            s   = sqrt(tmp)
            stddev[j] = (s <= eps ? 1.0 : s)

    # 3. Center and scale each column:
    #    data[i,j] <- (data[i,j] - mean[j]) / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    # We rewrite as a multiply by a precomputed per-column scale_j:
    #    scale_j = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[j]
    #    data[i,j] <- (data[i,j] - mean[j]) * scale_j
    # This removes an expensive sqrt and a divide from the inner loop.
    NORMALIZE:
        for j:
            scale_j = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[j]
            for i:
                data[i, j] = (data[i, j] - mean[j]) * scale_j

    # 4a. Set diagonal of the correlation matrix to 1.
    CORR_DIAG:
        for p:
            corr[p, p] = 1.0

    # 4b. Compute off-diagonal correlations.
    # After normalization, each column j of data has unit 2-norm, so
    #    corr[p, q] = sum_k data[k,p] * data[k,q]
    # is the correlation coefficient between variables p and q.
    # We only compute upper triangle (p < q) and mirror to enforce symmetry.
    CORR_OFFDIAG:
        for p, q:
            if p < q:
                corr[p, q] = sum(k, data[k, p] * data[k, q])
                corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]

dependencies:
    # Enforce the same phase ordering as in the original kernel.
    PRECOMPUTE -> MEAN
    MEAN       -> STDDEV
    STDDEV     -> NORMALIZE
    NORMALIZE  -> CORR_DIAG
    NORMALIZE  -> CORR_OFFDIAG

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Scalar and arithmetic optimizations
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # - PRECOMPUTE hoists 1/float_n, sqrt(float_n), and its inverse out of loops.
    # - NORMALIZE uses a per-column scale_j to replace per-element division by a
    #   multiply, and removes the SQRT_FUN(float_n) call from the inner loop.
    # These changes reduce the number of expensive sqrt/div operations by O(N*M).

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mean / stddev / normalization phases
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # For MEAN, STDDEV, and NORMALIZE, loops conceptually have the structure:
    #   for j in [0, M):
    #       for i in [0, N): ...
    # and reductions over i. With column-major layout, i is the contiguous dim.

    # Tile the observation dimension to improve cache reuse and enable
    # efficient vectorization on the innermost i-loops.
    block(i, Ii, Ti)             # i = Ii * Ti + i_inner

    # Vectorize reductions and normalization across the contiguous observation
    # index i. This maps naturally to SIMD loads/stores on data[i, j].
    vectorize(i, VF)

    # Parallelize over independent columns j for mean, stddev, and normalization.
    # Each j-column is updated and reduced independently, so no synchronization
    # is needed inside these loops.
    parallelize(j)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Correlation kernel: symmetric, tiled matrix multiplication D^T * D
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # CORR_OFFDIAG conceptually computes:
    #   for p in [0, M), q in [0, M), p < q:
    #       corr[p, q] = sum_k data[k, p] * data[k, q]
    # with data stored column-major. The heavy work is a symmetric
    # M x M product with an N-length reduction (gemm-like).

    # Block/tile the correlation dimensions (p, q) into tiles of size Tj, and
    # the reduction dimension k into tiles of size Tk to:
    #   - Increase temporal locality on data[k, p] and data[k, q]
    #   - Keep corr tiles in L1/L2 while accumulating over K-tiles
    block(p, P, Tj)              # p = P * Tj + p_inner
    block(q, Q, Tj)              # q = Q * Tj + q_inner
    block(k, K, Tk)              # k = K * Tk + k_inner

    # Hoist P, Q, and K to the outer levels so that:
    #   - Outer loops iterate over tiles (good units of parallel work)
    #   - Inner loops operate on small, cache-resident tiles and are reduction-
    #     friendly (sum over k_inner).
    hoist(P)
    hoist(Q)
    hoist(K)

    # Parallelize across correlation row-tiles P.
    # Each tile in P operates on a disjoint set of rows of corr, so no write–write
    # conflicts arise. The (p < q) condition ensures we never compute both (p,q)
    # and (q,p) in parallel.
    parallelize(P)

    # Vectorize over the reduction dimension k inside each (p, q) pair; with
    # column-major layout, k-indexed accesses data[k, p] and data[k, q] are
    # contiguous in memory.
    vectorize(k, VF)

    # Unroll the reduction loops over k to increase ILP and hide FMA latency.
    unroll(k, 4)

/**

/* correlation.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "correlation.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m,
		 int n,
		 DATA_TYPE *float_n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j;

  *float_n = (DATA_TYPE)N;

  for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < M; j++)
      data[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(i*j)/M + i;

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(corr,M,M,m,m))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("corr");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++) {
      if ((i * m + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, corr[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("corr");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_correlation[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
			DATA_TYPE float_n,
			DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m),
			DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(corr,M,M,m,m),
			DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(mean,M,m),
			DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(stddev,M,m))
{
  int i, j, k;

  DATA_TYPE eps = SCALAR_VAL(0.1);


#pragma scop
  for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
    {
      mean[j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
	mean[j] += data[i][j];
      mean[j] /= float_n;
    }


   for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
    {
      stddev[j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
        stddev[j] += (data[i][j] - mean[j]) * (data[i][j] - mean[j]);
      stddev[j] /= float_n;
      stddev[j] = SQRT_FUN(stddev[j]);
      /* The following in an inelegant but usual way to handle
         near-zero std. dev. values, which below would cause a zero-
         divide. */
      stddev[j] = stddev[j] <= eps ? SCALAR_VAL(1.0) : stddev[j];
    }

  /* Center and reduce the column vectors. */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
      {
        data[i][j] -= mean[j];
        data[i][j] /= SQRT_FUN(float_n) * stddev[j];
      }

  /* Calculate the m * m correlation matrix. */
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M-1; i++)
    {
      corr[i][i] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
      for (j = i+1; j < _PB_M; j++)
        {
          corr[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
          for (k = 0; k < _PB_N; k++)
            corr[i][j] += (data[k][i] * data[k][j]);
          corr[j][i] = corr[i][j];
        }
    }
  corr[_PB_M-1][_PB_M-1] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0);
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE float_n;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(data,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(corr,DATA_TYPE,M,M,m,m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(mean,DATA_TYPE,M,m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(stddev,DATA_TYPE,M,m);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n, &float_n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_correlation (m, n, float_n,
		      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data),
		      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(corr),
		      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(mean),
		      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(stddev));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(corr)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(data);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(corr);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(mean);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(stddev);

  return 0;
}

parameters:
    # Number of observations as a floating-point value.
    float_n: DATA_TYPE

    sqrt_n:      DATA_TYPE = sqrt(float_n)

          mean[j] = inv_float_n * sum(n, data[n, j])

    #    var_j    = (1 / float_n) * sum_n (data[n,j] - mean[j])^2
    #    stddev[j] = sqrt(var_j)
    #    stddev[j] = (stddev[j] <= eps ? 1.0 : stddev[j])
    #    scale[j]  = 1 / (sqrt_n * stddev[j])

    # (sum of squared deviations, then divide by N, then sqrt), but
    # avoids repeated division and sqrt in later phases.
    STDDEV_AND_SCALE:

          var_j    = inv_float_n *

      for j in j:
          for n in n:
              data[n, j] = (data[n, j] - mean[j]) * scale[j]

    # -------------------------

    # -------------------------

    #   varying n we get contiguous accesses in all three phases:
    #   MEAN, STDDEV_AND_SCALE, and NORMALIZE, as well as in CORR_OFFDIAGONAL.

    # Vectorize the reduction over n in MEAN, STDDEV_AND_SCALE, and the
    # inner products in CORR_OFFDIAGONAL, as well as the element-wise

    # ------------------------------------
    # In CORR_OFFDIAGONAL, each corr[p,q] is a dot product of two columns:
    #   corr[p,q] = sum_{n=0}^{N-1} data[n,p] * data[n,q]
    #
    # When N is large, blocking this reduction improves cache reuse by
    # operating on shorter column segments at a time while keeping the
    # corresponding corr[p,q] accumulators in registers or L1/L2.
    #

    # is then implemented as a sum over tiles K, each accumulating a
    # partial sum over a block of n.
    block(n, K, Tn_corr)

    # Inner-loop unrolling (micro-optimization)
    # ---------------------------------------
    # Unroll the innermost n-loop in the correlation kernel to reduce
    # loop-control overhead and expose more instruction-level parallelism.
    # This is particularly effective when combined with vectorization.
    unroll(n, 4)

    # 4. Scale data in-place.
    #    After this: data[i,j] = (raw[i,j] - mean[j]) / (sqrt(float_n)*stddev[j])
    #    Each column has variance 1/float_n and sum_i data[i,j]^2 = 1.
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    SCALE_DATA:
      for i:
        for j:
          data[i, j] = data[i, j] * inv_scale[j]

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Compute symmetric correlation matrix:
    #    corr[p,q] = sum_k data[k,p]*data[k,q], with corr[p,p] = 1.
    #    This is C = Z^T * Z for Z = normalized data, but we exploit symmetry
    #    and write only upper triangle, mirroring to lower.
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    CORR_DIAGONAL:
      for p:
        corr[p, p] = 1.0

    CORR_OFFDIAGONAL:
      for p:
        for q:
          if p < q:
            corr[p, q] = sum(k, data[k, p] * data[k, q])
            corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]

dependencies:
    # Mean must be fully computed before any use of mean[j].
    for j in [0, M):
      MEAN_INIT(j) -> MEAN_ACCUM(i, j)
      MEAN_ACCUM(i, j) -> MEAN_SCALE(j)

    # Variance accumulation and centering depend on finalized mean.
    for j in [0, M), i in [0, N):
      MEAN_SCALE(j) -> STDDEV_INIT(j)
      STDDEV_INIT(j) -> CENTER_AND_VAR(i, j)

    for j in [0, M):
      CENTER_AND_VAR(i, j) -> STDDEV_FINISH(j)

    # inv_scale[j] depends on finalized stddev[j] and float_n.
    for j in [0, M):
      STDDEV_FINISH(j) -> PREPARE_SCALE(j)

    # Scaling data depends on inv_scale[j] and centered data.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, M):
      PREPARE_SCALE(j) -> SCALE_DATA(i, j)

    # Correlation uses fully normalized data.
    for p in [0, M), q in [0, M), k in [0, N):
      SCALE_DATA(k, p) -> CORR_OFFDIAGONAL(p, q)
      SCALE_DATA(k, q) -> CORR_OFFDIAGONAL(p, q)

optimization:
    #==========================================================
    # High-level goals:
    #  - Use row-major (i,j) traversal for good cache locality.
    #  - Avoid repeated expensive operations: sqrt(float_n), division.
    #  - Expose parallelism over independent columns/column-pairs.
    #  - Map correlation to a tiled symmetric matrix multiply (Z^T * Z).
    #==========================================================

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # A) Data sweeps (MEAN_ACCUM, CENTER_AND_VAR, SCALE_DATA)
    #    over (i,j) space
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Use 2D blocking to improve cache reuse on data[i,j] and mean/stddev.
    block(i, I1, T_I_1)          # tile rows of data
    block(j, J1, T_J_1)          # tile columns of data
    hoist(I1)                    # outermost tile over rows
    hoist(J1)                    # next tile over columns

    # Vectorize along j, the contiguous dimension in row-major layout.
    vectorize(j, VEC_WIDTH)

    # Parallelize row-tiles across cores. For MEAN_ACCUM and CENTER_AND_VAR,
    # this implies a reduction on mean[j] and stddev[j], respectively.
    # + Operations are associative/commutative enough for FP reductions.
    parallelize(I1)

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # B) Correlation phase: corr = data^T * data (symmetric GEMM)
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Treat CORR_OFFDIAGONAL as a symmetric matrix multiplication of the
    # normalized data matrix with its transpose, with domain p < q.
    # Use 3D tiling over (p,q,k) to improve locality in both data and corr.
    block(p, P, T_P)             # tile over first variable index
    block(q, Q, T_Q)             # tile over second variable index
    block(k, K, T_K)             # tile over observation/reduction dimension

    hoist(P)
    hoist(Q)
    hoist(K)

    # Parallelize tiles of (P,Q): each tile updates a disjoint submatrix of corr.
    # The triangular constraint p < q is enforced inside tiles, so no races.
    parallelize(P)
    # Optionally, a runtime could "collapse" (P,Q) to 2D-parallelize.
    # (Not explicitly modeled; left to the backend.)

    # Vectorize along k in the innermost reduction loop, which has unit-stride
    # accesses in the first dimension of data[k, p] and data[k, q].
    vectorize(k, VEC_WIDTH)

    # Unroll the k-loop to improve ILP and better hide memory latency.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # C) Strength reduction and hoisting
    #----------------------------------------------------------
    # Already modeled explicitly in the computation:
    #  - PREPARE_SCALE hoists sqrt(float_n) out of all inner loops.
    #  - inv_scale[j] replaces N*M per-element divisions with:
    #        M per-column divisions + N*M multiplications.
    # No additional directives needed; code generators should map
    # PREPARE_SCALE + SCALE_DATA to scalar precomputation + SIMD muls.
--- END OF MODEL: correlation-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: correlation-03 ---
domain:
    # N: number of rows / observations
    # M: number of columns / variables
    n:  dim in [0, N)
    c:  dim in [0, M)
    c1: dim in [0, M)
    c2: dim in [0, M)

data:
    # Row-major 2D input, updated in-place to hold normalized data
    data[n, c]: inout DATA_TYPE = (n, c) -> n * M + c

    # Row-major 2D output: correlation matrix (M x M)
    corr[c1, c2]: out DATA_TYPE = (c1, c2) -> c1 * M + c2

    # 1D temporaries / outputs for each column
    mean[c]:   out  DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c
    stddev[c]: out  DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c

    # Additional 1D temporary: scaling factor per column.
    # scale[c] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[c]).
    # This costs only O(M) extra memory (< 50% overhead of original footprint).
    scale[c]:  tmp  DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c

parameters:
    float_n: in DATA_TYPE          # = (DATA_TYPE) N
    eps:     in DATA_TYPE          # = SCALAR_VAL(0.1)

    # Tuning parameters for the target x64 machine (to be chosen empirically)
    VEC_M:   in int                # vector width along contiguous column dimension
    TC:      in int                # tile size in column dimensions (for corr)
    TN:      in int                # tile size in row dimension (for corr)
    UC1:     in int                # unroll factor for c1 loop in corr
    UN:      in int                # unroll factor for n loop in corr

computation:

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Column means
    #    mean[c] = (1/float_n) * sum_n data[n, c]
    #    Implemented with row-major traversal (n outer, c inner).
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    mean_stage_init:
        for c:
            mean[c] = (DATA_TYPE)0.0

    mean_stage_accumulate:
        for n:
            for c:
                mean[c] += data[n, c]

    mean_stage_finalize:
        for c:
            mean[c] /= float_n

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Column standard deviations and per-column scaling factors
    #
    #    var[c]    = (1/float_n) * sum_n (data[n, c] - mean[c])^2
    #    stddev[c] = sqrt(var[c])
    #    if stddev[c] <= eps: stddev[c] = 1.0   (avoid division by ~0)
    #
    #    Precompute:
    #      sqrt_n      = sqrt(float_n)
    #      inv_sqrt_n  = 1 / sqrt_n
    #      scale[c]    = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[c]
    #
    #    scale[c] is later used to normalize data with only multiplies.
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    stddev_stage_init:
        for c:
            stddev[c] = (DATA_TYPE)0.0

    # Local scalars (conceptually hoisted once)
    sqrt_n:      scalar DATA_TYPE
    inv_sqrt_n:  scalar DATA_TYPE

    compute_sqrt_n:
        sqrt_n     = SQRT_FUN(float_n)
        inv_sqrt_n = ((DATA_TYPE)1.0) / sqrt_n

    stddev_stage_accumulate:
        for n:
            for c:
                tmp = data[n, c] - mean[c]
                stddev[c] += tmp * tmp

    stddev_stage_finalize:
        for c:
            stddev[c] /= float_n
            stddev[c]  = SQRT_FUN(stddev[c])
            stddev[c]  = stddev[c] <= eps ? (DATA_TYPE)1.0 : stddev[c]

            # scale[c] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[c])
            scale[c]   = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[c]

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Center and normalize the data in-place
    #
    #    data[n, c] <- (data[n, c] - mean[c]) * scale[c]
    #
    #    This matches the original:
    #      data -= mean; data /= sqrt(float_n) * stddev
    #    but uses one subtraction and two multiplies instead of
    #    repeated sqrt and division.
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    normalize_stage:
        for n:
            for c:
                data[n, c] = (data[n, c] - mean[c]) * scale[c]

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Correlation matrix on normalized data
    #
    #    For i != j:
    #      corr[i, j] = sum_n data[n, i] * data[n, j]
    #      corr[j, i] = corr[i, j]
    #    And corr[i, i] = 1.0 exactly.
    #
    #    We compute only the upper triangle via a symmetric
    #    rank-k update with row-major friendly traversal.
    #------------------------------------------------------------------

    # 4a. Initialize upper triangle (including diagonal) to 0
    corr_init:
        for c1:
            for c2 in [c1, M):
                corr[c1, c2] = (DATA_TYPE)0.0

    # 4b. Accumulate dot products:
    #     for each row n, update all (c1, c2 >= c1) pairs using that row.
    #
    #     This touches data[n, *] in row-major order and corr[* , *]
    #     in mostly row-major order (c2 innermost).
    corr_accum:
        for n:
            for c1:
                v1 = data[n, c1]
                for c2 in [c1, M):
                    corr[c1, c2] += v1 * data[n, c2]

    # 4c. Enforce symmetry and set diagonal exactly to 1.0
    corr_sym:
        for c1:
            corr[c1, c1] = (DATA_TYPE)1.0
            for c2 in [c1 + 1, M):
                corr[c2, c1] = corr[c1, c2]

optimization:

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mean and stddev computation: improve locality and exploit parallelism
    #------------------------------------------------------------------

    # Means:
    #  - As written, mean_stage_accumulate already uses (n outer, c inner),
    #    which matches row-major layout of data.
    #  - Parallelize across rows with a reduction on mean[c].
    mean_stage_accumulate: parallelize(n)          # reduction into mean[c]
    mean_stage_accumulate: vectorize(c, VEC_M)     # SIMD over contiguous columns

    # Stddev + scale:
    #  - Same row-major traversal.
    #  - Parallelize across n with reduction into stddev[c].
    stddev_stage_accumulate: parallelize(n)        # reduction into stddev[c]
    stddev_stage_accumulate: vectorize(c, VEC_M)

    # Finalization over columns is small; can be vectorized.
    stddev_stage_finalize: vectorize(c, VEC_M)

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Normalization: fully element-wise and embarrassingly parallel
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    normalize_stage: parallelize(n)
    normalize_stage: vectorize(c, VEC_M)

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Correlation accumulation: main hotspot
    #
    # Treat corr_accum as a symmetric rank-k update:
    #   corr += data^T * data   (upper triangle only).
    #
    # Strategy:
    #   - Tile both column dimensions (c1, c2) and the row dimension n.
    #   - Assign tile pairs (C1b, C2b) with C2b >= C1b to threads
    #     (no write sharing between threads).
    #   - Within each tile, traverse data row-major and corr row-major.
    #------------------------------------------------------------------

    # Tile column and row dimensions
    corr_accum: block(c1, C1b, TC)    # outer column tiles
    corr_accum: block(c2, C2b, TC)    # inner column tiles
    corr_accum: block(n,  Nb, TN)     # row tiles

    # Hoist tile loops to outermost levels
    corr_accum: hoist(C1b)
    corr_accum: hoist(C2b)
    corr_accum: hoist(Nb)

    # Parallelize over 2D column tiles.
    # Implementation must restrict to C2b >= C1b so only upper-triangular
    # tile pairs are computed, preserving original flop count.
    corr_accum: parallelize(C1b, C2b)

    # Within each tile:
    #   for Nb (rows in tile)
    #     for c1 in C1b
    #       v1 = data[n, c1]
    #       for c2 in C2b ∩ [c1, M)
    #         corr[c1, c2] += v1 * data[n, c2]
    #
    # Keep c2 as the innermost loop for contiguous accesses to corr and data.
    corr_accum: interchange(n, c1)        # order: Nb -> c1 -> n -> c2 or Nb -> n -> c1 -> c2
    corr_accum: interchange(c1, c2)       # ensure c2 is innermost within tile

    # Vectorize over c2 (contiguous in memory) and unroll small loops.
    corr_accum: vectorize(c2, VEC_M)
    corr_accum: unroll(c1, UC1)
    corr_accum: unroll(n,  UN)

    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Symmetrization and diagonal setup: cheap but parallelizable if desired
    #------------------------------------------------------------------
    corr_sym: parallelize(c1)
    corr_sym: vectorize(c2, VEC_M)
--- END OF MODEL: correlation-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: correlation-04 ---
domain:
    # Problem sizes (fixed at runtime via N, M)
    r: dim in [0, N)          # sample index (row of data)
    c: dim in [0, M)          # feature index / column of data
    p: dim in [0, M)          # row index of correlation matrix (feature index)
    q: dim in [0, M)          # column index of correlation matrix (feature index)
    k: dim in [0, N)          # reduction index over samples for correlation

data:
    # Input data matrix: N samples × M features, row-major as in C
    data[r, c]: inout DATA_TYPE = (r, c) -> r * M + c

    # Output correlation matrix: M × M, row-major
    corr[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q

    # Column-wise statistics
    mean[c]: inout DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c        # column means
    stddev[c]: inout DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c      # column standard deviations

    # Additional temporary scaling factors (small, O(M) memory)
    norm_factor[c]: temp DATA_TYPE = (c) -> c
        # = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[c]) after stddev has been clamped

parameters:
    # Problem dimensions (known at compile-time via macros N, M, but modeled as parameters)
    N: int
    M: int

    # Scalar parameters from the C code
    float_n: DATA_TYPE        # equals (DATA_TYPE) N
    eps: DATA_TYPE            # = 0.1, near-zero stddev threshold

    # Pre-hoisted scalar factors (computed once)
    inv_float_n: DATA_TYPE    # = 1.0 / float_n
    sqrt_float_n: DATA_TYPE   # = sqrt(float_n)

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen for the target machine)
    TILE_R: int               # tile size along r (rows of data)
    TILE_C: int               # tile size along c (columns of data)
    TILE_P: int               # tile size along p (corr rows / features)
    TILE_Q: int               # tile size along q (corr cols / features)
    TILE_K: int               # tile size along k (samples in corr reduction)
    VEC_WIDTH: int            # SIMD width in elements along contiguous dimensions
    UNROLL_R: int             # unroll factor along r
    UNROLL_C: int             # unroll factor along c
    UNROLL_P: int             # unroll factor along p (corr feature index)

computation:
    # 1. Compute column means:
    #    mean[c] = (1/float_n) * sum_r data[r, c]
    MEAN:
      # Initialize means
      for c:
        mean[c] = 0

      # Accumulate sums over rows
      for r:
        for c:
          mean[c] += data[r, c]

      # Scale by 1 / float_n
      for c:
        mean[c] *= inv_float_n

    # 2. Compute column standard deviations with near-zero handling:
    #    sigma2[c] = (1/float_n) * sum_r (data[r, c] - mean[c])^2
    #    s = sqrt(sigma2[c])
    #    stddev[c] = (s <= eps ? 1.0 : s)
    STDDEV:
      # Initialize variances to zero
      for c:
        stddev[c] = 0

      # Accumulate squared deviations
      for r:
        for c:
          let diff = data[r, c] - mean[c] in
            stddev[c] += diff * diff

      # Finalize stddev: divide by N, sqrt, and clamp to avoid division by near-zero
      for c:
        stddev[c] *= inv_float_n
        stddev[c] = sqrt(stddev[c])
        stddev[c] = (stddev[c] <= eps ? SCALAR_VAL(1.0) : stddev[c])

    # 3. Precompute normalized scaling factors per column:
    #    norm_factor[c] = 1 / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[c])
    # This replaces a division per element in the normalization step with
    # a multiplication by a precomputed factor.
    NORM_FACTOR:
      for c:
        norm_factor[c] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (sqrt_float_n * stddev[c])

    # 4. Center and reduce (normalize) the columns in-place:
    #    data[r, c] := (data[r, c] - mean[c]) * norm_factor[c]
    #
    # After this step, each column has zero mean and unit L2 norm, so that
    #   corr[p, q] = sum_r data[r, p] * data[r, q]
    # computes the correlation coefficients directly, and diag(corr) = 1.
    NORMALIZE:
      for r:
        for c:
          let centered = data[r, c] - mean[c] in
            data[r, c] = centered * norm_factor[c]

    # 5. Compute the m × m correlation matrix.
    #
    # Semantics (matching the original C kernel):
    #   - corr[p, p] = 1 for all p
    #   - for p < q:
    #         corr[p, q] = sum_r data[r, p] * data[r, q]
    #         corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]
    #
    # We express this as an upper-triangular reduction and an explicit
    # symmetrization step.
    CORR_UPPER:
      # Initialize upper triangle (including diagonal) to 0;
      # diagonal will be overwritten with 1 later.
      for p in [0, M):
        for q in [p, M):
          corr[p, q] = 0

      # Accumulate correlation via a symmetric rank‑k update:
      # rearranged loop order compared to the C code for better row reuse
      for k:
        for p in [0, M):
          let x = data[k, p] in
            for q in [p, M):
              corr[p, q] += x * data[k, q]

    CORR_SYMM:
      # Set diagonal to exactly 1 and copy upper triangle to lower triangle
      for p in [0, M):
        corr[p, p] = SCALAR_VAL(1.0)
        for q in [p + 1, M):
          corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]

dependencies:
    # High-level phase ordering (implied by data flow, made explicit here):
    for c in [0, M):
      MEAN -> STDDEV
      STDDEV -> NORM_FACTOR
      NORM_FACTOR -> NORMALIZE

    for p in [0, M), q in [p, M):
      NORMALIZE -> CORR_UPPER
      CORR_UPPER -> CORR_SYMM

optimization:
    # -------------------------------
    # General scalar hoisting
    # -------------------------------
    # Compute inv_float_n and sqrt_float_n once before all loops.
    # This removes repeated divisions and sqrt calls inside hot loops.
    hoist(inv_float_n)          # inv_float_n = 1.0 / float_n
    hoist(sqrt_float_n)         # sqrt_float_n = sqrt(float_n)

    # -------------------------------
    # Mean and stddev computation
    # -------------------------------
    # Accesses to data[r, c] are row-major contiguous in c,
    # so we tile and vectorize along c, and parallelize over tiles of r.
    block(r, R, TILE_R)
    block(c, C, TILE_C)

    # Within tiled loops:
    #   for R in ...
    #     parallel for r in R      # rows split across threads
    #       vectorized for c in C  # contiguous columns
    parallelize(R)
    vectorize(C, VEC_WIDTH)
    unroll(C, UNROLL_C)

    # Apply the same tiling and parallelization to STDDEV and NORMALIZE,
    # since they have the same iteration structure over (r, c).
    apply_to(STDDEV, NORMALIZE):
        block(r, R, TILE_R)
        block(c, C, TILE_C)
        parallelize(R)
        vectorize(C, VEC_WIDTH)
        unroll(C, UNROLL_C)

    # -------------------------------
    # Correlation accumulation (CORR_UPPER)
    # -------------------------------
    # Treat corr = data^T * data as a symmetric rank‑k update, but only
    # compute the upper triangle (p <= q). Use 3D blocking for better
    # cache reuse over data and corr, and to expose parallelism.
    block(k, K, TILE_K)         # tiles along the samples dimension
    block(p, P, TILE_P)         # tiles along correlation row (feature) index
    block(q, Q, TILE_Q)         # tiles along correlation col (feature) index

    # Order tiles as:
    #   for K:
    #     for P:
    #       for Q starting at P (only upper-triangular tiles):
    #         for k in K, p in P, q in [max(p, Q_start), Q_end):
    hoist(K)
    hoist(P)
    hoist(Q)

    # Parallelize over tiles of P (and/or Q) since each (p, q) in the upper
    # triangle is updated independently in the k-reduction.
    parallelize(P)

    # Within each tile, make q the innermost loop to benefit from contiguous
    # access to data[k, q] and corr[p, q].
    vectorize(q, VEC_WIDTH)
    unroll(p, UNROLL_P)

    # Optionally use a small on-chip temporary tile buffer corr_block[P, Q]
    # for each (P, Q) tile:
    #   - initialize corr_block to 0
    #   - accumulate over k in K into corr_block
    #   - write corr_block back to corr at the end of the (P, Q, K) tile
    # This buffer is of size TILE_P * TILE_Q and can be chosen so that
    #   TILE_P * TILE_Q * sizeof(DATA_TYPE)
    # stays well below 50% of the original total memory footprint.

    # -------------------------------
    # Correlation symmetrization (CORR_SYMM)
    # -------------------------------
    # The symmetrization step writes corr[q, p] = corr[p, q] for p < q
    # and sets corr[p, p] = 1. Each (p, q) pair is independent, so we
    # parallelize over p and vectorize over q.
    parallelize(p)
    vectorize(q, VEC_WIDTH)
    unroll(p, UNROLL_P)
--- END OF MODEL: correlation-04 ---

--- START OF MODEL: correlation-05 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)          # observation index (rows of data)
    j: dim in [0, M)          # variable index (columns of data)
    p: dim in [0, M)          # row index of correlation matrix
    q: dim in [0, M)          # column index of correlation matrix
    k: dim in [0, N)          # reduction index over observations

data:
    # Store data column-major so that scans over i/k are contiguous in memory.
    # This matches all heavy inner loops (means, stddev, normalization, correlation),
    # which iterate over observations for a fixed column/variable.
    data[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> j * N + i
        # Column-major: each column j is stored as a contiguous N-element vector

    mean[j]:   inout DATA_TYPE = j -> j        # per-variable mean
    stddev[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = j -> j        # per-variable stddev (after epsilon clamp)

    corr[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q
        # Row-major correlation matrix, as in the original C code

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE    # N as a floating-point value
    eps: DATA_TYPE        # small epsilon avoiding division by tiny stddevs

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    Ti: int               # tile size in observation dimension (i, k) for all reductions
    Tj: int               # tile size in variable / correlation dimensions (j, p, q)
    Tk: int               # tile size in reduction dimension k for correlation
    VF: int               # vector width for innermost loops (e.g., 4 or 8 for x86_64)

computation:
    # Hoist scalar computations that are invariant across all loops.
    PRECOMPUTE:
        inv_n      = 1.0 / float_n              # used in mean and variance
        sqrt_n     = sqrt(float_n)              # SQRT_FUN(float_n) in original code
        inv_sqrt_n = 1.0 / sqrt_n               # used in normalization

    # 1. Compute column means: mean[j] = (1/N) * sum_i data[i,j]
    MEAN:
        for j:
            mean[j] = inv_n * sum(i, data[i, j])

    # 2. Compute standard deviations (with epsilon guard):
    #    stddev[j] = sqrt( (1/N) * sum_i (data[i,j] - mean[j])^2 )
    #    if stddev[j] <= eps then stddev[j] = 1.0
    STDDEV:
        for j:
            tmp = sum(i, (data[i, j] - mean[j]) * (data[i, j] - mean[j]))
            tmp = inv_n * tmp
            s   = sqrt(tmp)
            stddev[j] = (s <= eps ? 1.0 : s)

    # 3. Center and scale each column:
    #    data[i,j] <- (data[i,j] - mean[j]) / (sqrt(float_n) * stddev[j])
    # We rewrite as a multiply by a precomputed per-column scale_j:
    #    scale_j = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[j]
    #    data[i,j] <- (data[i,j] - mean[j]) * scale_j
    # This removes an expensive sqrt and a divide from the inner loop.
    NORMALIZE:
        for j:
            scale_j = inv_sqrt_n / stddev[j]
            for i:
                data[i, j] = (data[i, j] - mean[j]) * scale_j

    # 4a. Set diagonal of the correlation matrix to 1.
    CORR_DIAG:
        for p:
            corr[p, p] = 1.0

    # 4b. Compute off-diagonal correlations.
    # After normalization, each column j of data has unit 2-norm, so
    #    corr[p, q] = sum_k data[k,p] * data[k,q]
    # is the correlation coefficient between variables p and q.
    # We only compute upper triangle (p < q) and mirror to enforce symmetry.
    CORR_OFFDIAG:
        for p, q:
            if p < q:
                corr[p, q] = sum(k, data[k, p] * data[k, q])
                corr[q, p] = corr[p, q]

dependencies:
    # Enforce the same phase ordering as in the original kernel.
    PRECOMPUTE -> MEAN
    MEAN       -> STDDEV
    STDDEV     -> NORMALIZE
    NORMALIZE  -> CORR_DIAG
    NORMALIZE  -> CORR_OFFDIAG

optimization:
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Scalar and arithmetic optimizations
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # - PRECOMPUTE hoists 1/float_n, sqrt(float_n), and its inverse out of loops.
    # - NORMALIZE uses a per-column scale_j to replace per-element division by a
    #   multiply, and removes the SQRT_FUN(float_n) call from the inner loop.
    # These changes reduce the number of expensive sqrt/div operations by O(N*M).

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mean / stddev / normalization phases
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # For MEAN, STDDEV, and NORMALIZE, loops conceptually have the structure:
    #   for j in [0, M):
    #       for i in [0, N): ...
    # and reductions over i. With column-major layout, i is the contiguous dim.

    # Tile the observation dimension to improve cache reuse and enable
    # efficient vectorization on the innermost i-loops.
    block(i, Ii, Ti)             # i = Ii * Ti + i_inner

    # Vectorize reductions and normalization across the contiguous observation
    # index i. This maps naturally to SIMD loads/stores on data[i, j].
    vectorize(i, VF)

    # Parallelize over independent columns j for mean, stddev, and normalization.
    # Each j-column is updated and reduced independently, so no synchronization
    # is needed inside these loops.
    parallelize(j)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Correlation kernel: symmetric, tiled matrix multiplication D^T * D
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # CORR_OFFDIAG conceptually computes:
    #   for p in [0, M), q in [0, M), p < q:
    #       corr[p, q] = sum_k data[k, p] * data[k, q]
    # with data stored column-major. The heavy work is a symmetric
    # M x M product with an N-length reduction (gemm-like).

    # Block/tile the correlation dimensions (p, q) into tiles of size Tj, and
    # the reduction dimension k into tiles of size Tk to:
    #   - Increase temporal locality on data[k, p] and data[k, q]
    #   - Keep corr tiles in L1/L2 while accumulating over K-tiles
    block(p, P, Tj)              # p = P * Tj + p_inner
    block(q, Q, Tj)              # q = Q * Tj + q_inner
    block(k, K, Tk)              # k = K * Tk + k_inner

    # Hoist P, Q, and K to the outer levels so that:
    #   - Outer loops iterate over tiles (good units of parallel work)
    #   - Inner loops operate on small, cache-resident tiles and are reduction-
    #     friendly (sum over k_inner).
    hoist(P)
    hoist(Q)
    hoist(K)

    # Parallelize across correlation row-tiles P.
    # Each tile in P operates on a disjoint set of rows of corr, so no write–write
    # conflicts arise. The (p < q) condition ensures we never compute both (p,q)
    # and (q,p) in parallel.
    parallelize(P)

    # Vectorize over the reduction dimension k inside each (p, q) pair; with
    # column-major layout, k-indexed accesses data[k, p] and data[k, q] are
    # contiguous in memory.
    vectorize(k, VF)

    # Unroll the reduction loops over k to increase ILP and hide FMA latency.
    unroll(k, 4)

/* covariance.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "covariance.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE *float_n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j;

  *float_n = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < M; j++)
      data[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*j) / M;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(cov,M,M,m,m))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("cov");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++) {
      if ((i * m + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, cov[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("cov");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_covariance[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		       DATA_TYPE float_n,
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m),
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(cov,M,M,m,m),
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(mean,M,m))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
    {
      mean[j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
        mean[j] += data[i][j];
      mean[j] /= float_n;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
      data[i][j] -= mean[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    for (j = i; j < _PB_M; j++)
      {
        cov[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
        for (k = 0; k < _PB_N; k++)
	  cov[i][j] += data[k][i] * data[k][j];
        cov[i][j] /= (float_n - SCALAR_VAL(1.0));
        cov[j][i] = cov[i][j];
      }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE float_n;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(data,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(cov,DATA_TYPE,M,M,m,m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(mean,DATA_TYPE,M,m);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n, &float_n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_covariance (m, n, float_n,
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data),
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(cov),
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(mean));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(cov)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(data);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(cov);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(mean);

  return 0;
}

# Optimized model for PolyBench/C covariance kernel

domain:
    i_n: dim in [0, N)                # row index for 'data' (observations)
    j_m: dim in [0, M)                # column index / feature index
    p:   dim in [0, M)                # covariance row index (feature)
    q:   dim in [0, M)                # covariance column index (feature), with q >= p in loops

data:
    # data: N x M matrix, row-major
    data[i_n, j_m]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i_n, j_m) -> i_n * M + j_m

    # cov: M x M covariance matrix, row-major
    cov[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q

    # mean: per-column means, length M
    mean[j_m]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j_m) -> j_m

parameters:
    N: int
    M: int
    float_n: DATA_TYPE                # equals (DATA_TYPE) N at run time

    # Tunable blocking and SIMD parameters (for cache/SIMD tuning on the target x64 machine)
    TI: int                           # tile size in row (N) dimension, e.g., 64..256
    TJ: int                           # tile size in column (M) dimension for data, e.g., 32..128
    TP: int                           # tile size in covariance row dimension p, e.g., 16..64
    TQ: int                           # tile size in covariance col dimension q, e.g., 16..64
    TK: int                           # optional tile size in row dimension i_n for covariance, e.g., 64..512
    VEC_M: int                        # SIMD width for operations along j_m / q (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles)

computation:
    # 1. Compute per-column means.
    #    Loops are organized to stream 'data' row-major (i_n outer, j_m inner).
    #    For each fixed column j_m, the sequence of additions over i_n is the
    #    same as in the original code (only interleaved with updates to other
    #    columns), so each mean[j_m] is bitwise identical to the original.
    MEAN_INIT:
    for j_m in [0, M):
        mean[j_m] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0)

    MEAN_ACCUM:
    for i_n in [0, N):
        for j_m in [0, M):
            mean[j_m] += data[i_n, j_m]

    MEAN_SCALE:
    for j_m in [0, M):
        mean[j_m] /= float_n

    # 2. Center the data matrix in-place: subtract the column means.
    CENTER_DATA:
    for i_n in [0, N):
        for j_m in [0, M):
            data[i_n, j_m] -= mean[j_m]

    # 3. Initialize the upper triangle of the covariance matrix to zero.
    COV_INIT:
    for p in [0, M):
        for q in [p, M):              # upper triangle including diagonal
            cov[p, q] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0)

    # 4. Accumulate covariance row-by-row to maximize reuse of each row of 'data'.
    #    For each centered observation (row i_n), update all cov[p, q] with p <= q.
    #    For any fixed pair (p0, q0), the sequence of additions to cov[p0, q0]
    #    over i_n is in the same order as in the original code; only operations
    #    on other entries are interleaved.
    COV_ACCUM:
    for i_n in [0, N):
        for p in [0, M):
            for q in [p, M):
                cov[p, q] += data[i_n, p] * data[i_n, q]

    # 5. Scale by (float_n - 1.0) and mirror the upper triangle to the lower.
    COV_SCALE_AND_SYMMETRIZE:
    for p in [0, M):
        for q in [p, M):
            cov[p, q] /= (float_n - SCALAR_VAL(1.0))
            cov[q, p] = cov[p, q]

dependencies:
    # Mean computation phases must be ordered:
    for j_m in [0, M):
        MEAN_INIT(j_m) -> MEAN_ACCUM(i_n, j_m)
        MEAN_ACCUM(i_n, j_m) -> MEAN_SCALE(j_m)

    # Centering uses the final means:
    for i_n in [0, N), j_m in [0, M):
        MEAN_SCALE(j_m) -> CENTER_DATA(i_n, j_m)

    # Covariance uses the centered data; initialization must precede accumulation:
    for p in [0, M), q in [p, M), i_n in [0, N):
        CENTER_DATA(i_n, p) -> COV_INIT(p, q)
        COV_INIT(p, q) -> COV_ACCUM(i_n, p, q)

    # Scaling/symmetrization acts on the fully accumulated covariance:
    for p in [0, M), q in [p, M), i_n in [0, N):
        COV_ACCUM(i_n, p, q) -> COV_SCALE_AND_SYMMETRIZE(p, q)

optimization:
    #-------------------------------
    # 1. Improve memory locality
    #-------------------------------
    # a) Mean accumulation and centering already stream 'data' row-major
    #    (i_n outer, j_m inner), which is optimal for its row-major layout.

    # b) Covariance accumulation has been reorganized (relative to the original
    #    i/j/k nest) to use i_n (row index) as the outermost loop. Each row
    #    data[i_n, *] is loaded once and reused across all (p, q) pairs before
    #    moving to the next row, improving temporal locality compared to
    #    revisiting the entire data set for each (i, j) column pair.

    # Tile the row and column dimensions to keep working sets in L1/L2 caches.
    # These tiles are shared across all loop nests over the same logical dims.
    block(i_n, I_N, TI)              # tile rows of 'data' where beneficial
    block(j_m, J_M, TJ)              # tile columns for MEAN_ACCUM and CENTER_DATA
    block(p,   P,   TP)              # tile covariance row index
    block(q,   Q,   TQ)              # tile covariance column index within [p, M)
    block(i_n, K_N, TK)              # optional additional tiling of i_n in COV_ACCUM

    #-------------------------------
    # 2. Parallelization
    #-------------------------------
    # a) Centering: independent updates per row of 'data'.
    parallelize(I_N)                 # parallelize CENTER_DATA over blocks of i_n

    # b) Mean accumulation: reduction over i_n for each j_m.
    #    Semantically: mean[j_m] = (1/float_n) * sum_{i_n} data[i_n, j_m].
    #    A parallel implementation can use a reduction on mean[j_m] or
    #    thread-private partial mean vectors.
    parallelize(I_N)                 # parallelize MEAN_ACCUM over i_n with reduction on mean[j_m]

    # c) Covariance accumulation: parallelize over p (feature index).
    #    For fixed i_n, each (p, q) pair is uniquely owned by a single p,
    #    so 'parallelize(p)' introduces no write conflicts on cov[p, q].
    parallelize(P)                   # in COV_ACCUM, parallelize outer P tiles over threads

    # d) Final scaling and symmetrization: independent per (p, q) with p <= q.
    parallelize(P)                   # parallelize COV_SCALE_AND_SYMMETRIZE over P tiles

    #-------------------------------
    # 3. SIMD vectorization and unrolling
    #-------------------------------
    # Exploit contiguous access in the column dimension (inner loops in j_m / q).
    vectorize(J_M, VEC_M)            # vectorize inner j_m loops in MEAN_ACCUM and CENTER_DATA
    vectorize(Q,   VEC_M)            # vectorize inner q loops in COV_ACCUM and COV_SCALE_AND_SYMMETRIZE

    # Optional modest unrolling of short loops over p to increase ILP.
    unroll(p, 2)

    #-------------------------------
    # 4. Arithmetic optimizations
    #-------------------------------
    # Precompute reciprocals to replace repeated divisions by constants
    # with multiplications (optional if tiny rounding differences are acceptable):
    #   inv_float_n        = 1.0 / float_n
    #   inv_float_n_minus1 = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)
    # and then:
    #   mean[j_m] *= inv_float_n
    #   cov[p, q] *= inv_float_n_minus1
    #
    # This removes O(M + M^2) scalar divisions from the steady-state kernel.
    # If bitwise-exact results are required, keep the divisions and omit this step.
