/* covariance.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "covariance.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE *float_n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j;

  *float_n = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < M; j++)
      data[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*j) / M;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(cov,M,M,m,m))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("cov");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++) {
      if ((i * m + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, cov[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("cov");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_covariance[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		       DATA_TYPE float_n,
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m),
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(cov,M,M,m,m),
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(mean,M,m))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
    {
      mean[j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
        mean[j] += data[i][j];
      mean[j] /= float_n;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
      data[i][j] -= mean[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    for (j = i; j < _PB_M; j++)
      {
        cov[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
        for (k = 0; k < _PB_N; k++)
	  cov[i][j] += data[k][i] * data[k][j];
        cov[i][j] /= (float_n - SCALAR_VAL(1.0));
        cov[j][i] = cov[i][j];
      }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE float_n;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(data,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(cov,DATA_TYPE,M,M,m,m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(mean,DATA_TYPE,M,m);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n, &float_n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_covariance (m, n, float_n,
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data),
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(cov),
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(mean));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(cov)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(data);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(cov);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(mean);

  return 0;
}

# Optimized model for PolyBench/C covariance kernel

domain:
    i_n: dim in [0, N)                # row index for 'data' (observations)
    j_m: dim in [0, M)                # column index / feature index
    p:   dim in [0, M)                # covariance row index (feature)
    q:   dim in [0, M)                # covariance column index (feature), with q >= p in loops

data:
    # data: N x M matrix, row-major
    data[i_n, j_m]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i_n, j_m) -> i_n * M + j_m

    # cov: M x M covariance matrix, row-major
    cov[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q

    # mean: per-column means, length M
    mean[j_m]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j_m) -> j_m

parameters:
    N: int
    M: int
    float_n: DATA_TYPE                # equals (DATA_TYPE) N at run time

    # Tunable blocking and SIMD parameters (for cache/SIMD tuning on the target x64 machine)
    TI: int                           # tile size in row (N) dimension, e.g., 64..256
    TJ: int                           # tile size in column (M) dimension for data, e.g., 32..128
    TP: int                           # tile size in covariance row dimension p, e.g., 16..64
    TQ: int                           # tile size in covariance col dimension q, e.g., 16..64
    TK: int                           # optional tile size in row dimension i_n for covariance, e.g., 64..512
    VEC_M: int                        # SIMD width for operations along j_m / q (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles)

computation:
    # 1. Compute per-column means.
    #    Loops are organized to stream 'data' row-major (i_n outer, j_m inner).
    #    For each fixed column j_m, the sequence of additions over i_n is the
    #    same as in the original code (only interleaved with updates to other
    #    columns), so each mean[j_m] is bitwise identical to the original.
    MEAN_INIT:
    for j_m in [0, M):
        mean[j_m] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0)

    MEAN_ACCUM:
    for i_n in [0, N):
        for j_m in [0, M):
            mean[j_m] += data[i_n, j_m]

    MEAN_SCALE:
    for j_m in [0, M):
        mean[j_m] /= float_n

    # 2. Center the data matrix in-place: subtract the column means.
    CENTER_DATA:
    for i_n in [0, N):
        for j_m in [0, M):
            data[i_n, j_m] -= mean[j_m]

    # 3. Initialize the upper triangle of the covariance matrix to zero.
    COV_INIT:
    for p in [0, M):
        for q in [p, M):              # upper triangle including diagonal
            cov[p, q] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0)

    # 4. Accumulate covariance row-by-row to maximize reuse of each row of 'data'.
    #    For each centered observation (row i_n), update all cov[p, q] with p <= q.
    #    For any fixed pair (p0, q0), the sequence of additions to cov[p0, q0]
    #    over i_n is in the same order as in the original code; only operations
    #    on other entries are interleaved.
    COV_ACCUM:
    for i_n in [0, N):
        for p in [0, M):
            for q in [p, M):
                cov[p, q] += data[i_n, p] * data[i_n, q]

    # 5. Scale by (float_n - 1.0) and mirror the upper triangle to the lower.
    COV_SCALE_AND_SYMMETRIZE:
    for p in [0, M):
        for q in [p, M):
            cov[p, q] /= (float_n - SCALAR_VAL(1.0))
            cov[q, p] = cov[p, q]

dependencies:
    # Mean computation phases must be ordered:
    for j_m in [0, M):
        MEAN_INIT(j_m) -> MEAN_ACCUM(i_n, j_m)
        MEAN_ACCUM(i_n, j_m) -> MEAN_SCALE(j_m)

    # Centering uses the final means:
    for i_n in [0, N), j_m in [0, M):
        MEAN_SCALE(j_m) -> CENTER_DATA(i_n, j_m)

    # Covariance uses the centered data; initialization must precede accumulation:
    for p in [0, M), q in [p, M), i_n in [0, N):
        CENTER_DATA(i_n, p) -> COV_INIT(p, q)
        COV_INIT(p, q) -> COV_ACCUM(i_n, p, q)

    # Scaling/symmetrization acts on the fully accumulated covariance:
    for p in [0, M), q in [p, M), i_n in [0, N):
        COV_ACCUM(i_n, p, q) -> COV_SCALE_AND_SYMMETRIZE(p, q)

optimization:
    #-------------------------------
    # 1. Improve memory locality
    #-------------------------------
    # a) Mean accumulation and centering already stream 'data' row-major
    #    (i_n outer, j_m inner), which is optimal for its row-major layout.

    # b) Covariance accumulation has been reorganized (relative to the original
    #    i/j/k nest) to use i_n (row index) as the outermost loop. Each row
    #    data[i_n, *] is loaded once and reused across all (p, q) pairs before
    #    moving to the next row, improving temporal locality compared to
    #    revisiting the entire data set for each (i, j) column pair.

    # Tile the row and column dimensions to keep working sets in L1/L2 caches.
    # These tiles are shared across all loop nests over the same logical dims.
    block(i_n, I_N, TI)              # tile rows of 'data' where beneficial
    block(j_m, J_M, TJ)              # tile columns for MEAN_ACCUM and CENTER_DATA
    block(p,   P,   TP)              # tile covariance row index
    block(q,   Q,   TQ)              # tile covariance column index within [p, M)
    block(i_n, K_N, TK)              # optional additional tiling of i_n in COV_ACCUM

    #-------------------------------
    # 2. Parallelization
    #-------------------------------
    # a) Centering: independent updates per row of 'data'.
    parallelize(I_N)                 # parallelize CENTER_DATA over blocks of i_n

    # b) Mean accumulation: reduction over i_n for each j_m.
    #    Semantically: mean[j_m] = (1/float_n) * sum_{i_n} data[i_n, j_m].
    #    A parallel implementation can use a reduction on mean[j_m] or
    #    thread-private partial mean vectors.
    parallelize(I_N)                 # parallelize MEAN_ACCUM over i_n with reduction on mean[j_m]

    # c) Covariance accumulation: parallelize over p (feature index).
    #    For fixed i_n, each (p, q) pair is uniquely owned by a single p,
    #    so 'parallelize(p)' introduces no write conflicts on cov[p, q].
    parallelize(P)                   # in COV_ACCUM, parallelize outer P tiles over threads

    # d) Final scaling and symmetrization: independent per (p, q) with p <= q.
    parallelize(P)                   # parallelize COV_SCALE_AND_SYMMETRIZE over P tiles

    #-------------------------------
    # 3. SIMD vectorization and unrolling
    #-------------------------------
    # Exploit contiguous access in the column dimension (inner loops in j_m / q).
    vectorize(J_M, VEC_M)            # vectorize inner j_m loops in MEAN_ACCUM and CENTER_DATA
    vectorize(Q,   VEC_M)            # vectorize inner q loops in COV_ACCUM and COV_SCALE_AND_SYMMETRIZE

    # Optional modest unrolling of short loops over p to increase ILP.
    unroll(p, 2)

    #-------------------------------
    # 4. Arithmetic optimizations
    #-------------------------------
    # Precompute reciprocals to replace repeated divisions by constants
    # with multiplications (optional if tiny rounding differences are acceptable):
    #   inv_float_n        = 1.0 / float_n
    #   inv_float_n_minus1 = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)
    # and then:
    #   mean[j_m] *= inv_float_n
    #   cov[p, q] *= inv_float_n_minus1
    #
    # This removes O(M + M^2) scalar divisions from the steady-state kernel.
    # If bitwise-exact results are required, keep the divisions and omit this step.
--- END OF MODEL: covariance-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: covariance-02 ---
# Optimized model for covariance.c

domain:
    # N: number of observations (rows in 'data')
    # M: number of variables / features (columns in 'data')
    i: dim in [0, N)          # observation index
    j: dim in [0, M)          # feature index
    p: dim in [0, M)          # covariance row (feature)
    q: dim in [0, M)          # covariance column (feature)
    k: dim in [0, N)          # reduction index over observations

data:
    # Original layout from PolyBench: row-major N x M
    data[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * M + j
        # data[i, j] is the j-th feature of the i-th observation.
        # It is modified in-place to hold centered data (zero-mean per column).

    cov[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q
        # Full M x M covariance matrix, symmetric in (p, q).

    mean[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j
        # Mean of each feature j over all N observations.

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE              # number of observations, as a scalar
    inv_n: DATA_TYPE                # = 1.0 / float_n
    inv_n_minus_1: DATA_TYPE        # = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)

    # Tuning / blocking parameters (chosen to respect cache and memory limits)
    BM: int                         # feature tile size (e.g., 32 or 64)
    BN: int                         # observation tile size for covariance (e.g., 128 or 256)

computation:
    #---------------------------------------------
    # Stage 0: precompute reciprocals
    #---------------------------------------------
    PRE_INV:
        inv_n = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / float_n
        inv_n_minus_1 = SCALAR_VAL(1.0) / (float_n - SCALAR_VAL(1.0))

    #---------------------------------------------
    # Stage 1: compute per-feature mean
    #  Original:
    #    for j:
    #      mean[j] = 0
    #      for i: mean[j] += data[i][j];
    #      mean[j] /= float_n;
    #  Optimized:
    #    - Separate initialization, accumulation, and scaling.
    #    - Accumulate in row-major order (i outer, j inner) for better locality.
    #---------------------------------------------
    MEAN_INIT:
        for j:
            mean[j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0)

    MEAN_ACCUM:
        for i, j:
            mean[j] += data[i, j]

    MEAN_SCALE:
        for j:
            mean[j] *= inv_n

    #---------------------------------------------
    # Stage 2: center data in-place
    #  data[i, j] <- data[i, j] - mean[j]
    #  (same as original second loop nest)
    #---------------------------------------------
    CENTER:
        for i, j:
            data[i, j] -= mean[j]

    #---------------------------------------------
    # Stage 3: covariance of centered data
    #
    # Mathematical definition:
    #   cov[p, q] = 1 / (float_n - 1) *
    #               sum_{k=0..N-1} data[k, p] * data[k, q]
    #
    # We exploit symmetry (cov[p, q] == cov[q, p]) and only
    # compute the upper triangle p <= q, then mirror.
    #---------------------------------------------

    # 3a. Compute upper-triangular covariance values
    COV_UPPER:
        for p in [0, M), q in [p, M):
            cov[p, q] = inv_n_minus_1 * sum(k in [0, N), data[k, p] * data[k, q])

    # 3b. Mirror upper triangle into lower triangle
    COV_MIRROR:
        for p in [0, M), q in [p+1, M):
            cov[q, p] = cov[p, q]

dependencies:
    # Mean must be fully computed before centering, and centering must
    # complete before covariance is computed.

    # Mean computation pipeline per feature j:
    for j in [0, M):
        MEAN_INIT(j) -> MEAN_ACCUM(*, j) -> MEAN_SCALE(j) -> CENTER(*, j)

    # Centered data is required before covariance:
    for p in [0, M), q in [p, M):
        CENTER(*, p) -> COV_UPPER(p, q)
        CENTER(*, q) -> COV_UPPER(p, q)

    # Mirroring uses results of upper triangle:
    for p in [0, M), q in [p+1, M):
        COV_UPPER(p, q) -> COV_MIRROR(p, q)

optimization:
    #------------------------------------------------
    # General scalar optimizations
    #------------------------------------------------
    # Precompute reciprocals once, instead of dividing inside loops.
    # This replaces many divisions with cheaper multiplications.
    hoist(PRE_INV)

    #------------------------------------------------
    # Mean computation (MEAN_INIT, MEAN_ACCUM, MEAN_SCALE)
    #------------------------------------------------
    # Accumulate mean in row-major order: (i, j).
    # Original code was column-wise (j outer, i inner) and stride-M.
    # The new order improves spatial locality on 'data'.
    interchange(i, j) in MEAN_ACCUM

    # Parallelize accumulation over rows 'i'; each thread updates the
    # shared mean[j] using reductions across i.
    # (Implementation would use a reduction or privatization scheme.)
    parallelize(i) in MEAN_ACCUM

    # Exploit SIMD along contiguous feature dimension j.
    vectorize(j, VF_MEAN) in MEAN_ACCUM      # VF_MEAN: SIMD width (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles)
    unroll(j, UF_MEAN) in MEAN_ACCUM        # UF_MEAN: small unroll factor (e.g., 2–4)

    # Initialization and scaling of mean are cheap; just parallelize over j.
    parallelize(j) in MEAN_INIT
    parallelize(j) in MEAN_SCALE
    vectorize(j, VF_MEAN) in MEAN_INIT
    vectorize(j, VF_MEAN) in MEAN_SCALE

    #------------------------------------------------
    # Centering (CENTER)
    #------------------------------------------------
    # CENTER already traverses data in row-major order (i, j).
    # Parallelize across independent rows and vectorize across columns.
    parallelize(i) in CENTER
    vectorize(j, VF_CENTER) in CENTER       # VF_CENTER: SIMD width for DATA_TYPE
    unroll(j, UF_CENTER) in CENTER

    #------------------------------------------------
    # Covariance computation (COV_UPPER)
    #------------------------------------------------
    # Realize the reduction in COV_UPPER in an outer-product style:
    #
    #   for p, q with p <= q:
    #       cov[p, q] = 0
    #   for k in [0, N):
    #       for p in [0, M):
    #           for q in [p, M):
    #               cov[p, q] += inv_n_minus_1 * data[k, p] * data[k, q]
    #
    # This:
    #   - Traverses 'data' row-wise (k fixed, p/q varying), making
    #     accesses to data[k, *] contiguous in memory.
    #   - Exposes a rank-1 update (outer product) structure similar to SYRK.
    #
    hoist(k) in COV_UPPER        # Move k to be the outermost loop of the reduction
    interchange(k, p) in COV_UPPER
    interchange(p, q) in COV_UPPER

    # Block over feature dimensions (p, q) and observation dimension k to
    # keep the working set of each tile in L2 cache.
    #
    # For each tile:
    #   - We operate on BM features in both p and q dimensions.
    #   - We process BN observations (k) at a time.
    #
    # Working set per tile ~ O(BM^2 + BM*BN) elements, tuned via BM, BN.
    block(p, P, BM) in COV_UPPER    # P: tile index for p
    block(q, Q, BM) in COV_UPPER    # Q: tile index for q
    block(k, K, BN) in COV_UPPER    # K: tile index for k

    # Hoist tile loops outwards for better reuse.
    hoist(P) in COV_UPPER
    hoist(Q) in COV_UPPER
    hoist(K) in COV_UPPER

    # Within each (P, Q, K) tile, only compute (p, q) with p <= q.
    # This preserves triangular domain while still using rectangular
    # tiles internally; out-of-domain (p, q) in a tile are skipped.
    # (Conceptually: masked computation inside each tile.)
    #   # no explicit syntax, but implied by original domain p <= q

    # Parallelization:
    #   - Each (P, Q) tile in the upper triangle is independent.
    #   - Parallelizing over P distributes row blocks of the covariance
    #     matrix across cores.
    parallelize(P) in COV_UPPER

    # Vectorization:
    #   - For fixed K, P, and p, the innermost loop over q accesses
    #     data[k, q] and cov[p, q] with unit stride.
    #   - Vectorize along q to use wide SIMD loads/stores.
    vectorize(q, VF_COV) in COV_UPPER
    unroll(q, UF_COV) in COV_UPPER

    # (Optional) Further unrolling/vectorization over k inside tiles
    # can be applied if the compiler supports efficient strided SIMD
    # or if additional packing is introduced.
    # vectorize(k, VF_COV_K) in COV_UPPER
    # unroll(k, UF_COV_K) in COV_UPPER

    #------------------------------------------------
    # Covariance mirroring (COV_MIRROR)
    #------------------------------------------------
    # COV_MIRROR touches each off-diagonal element exactly once.
    # It is embarrassingly parallel over p (or q) and trivially vectorizable.
    parallelize(p) in COV_MIRROR
    vectorize(q, VF_SCALE) in COV_MIRROR
    unroll(q, UF_SCALE) in COV_MIRROR

    #------------------------------------------------
    # Summary of tunable factors:
    #   BM, BN          : tile sizes for features and observations
    #   VF_*            : SIMD widths (usually match hardware vector width)
    #   UF_*            : small unroll factors (2–8) guided by microarchitecture
    #
    # These parameters can be tuned for the specific x64 machine and
    # compiler to maximize performance while preserving the original
    # numerical computation of the covariance.
--- END OF MODEL: covariance-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: covariance-03 ---
domain:
    # N: number of observations (rows)
    # M: number of variables / features (columns)
    i: dim in [0, N)          # observation index (row of data)
    j: dim in [0, M)          # feature index (column of data / mean)
    p: dim in [0, M)          # covariance row index
    q: dim in [0, M)          # covariance column index
    k: dim in [0, N)          # reduction index over observations

data:
    # Data matrix: N x M.
    # Layout chosen to match the kernel’s column-wise traversals (mean & covariance).
    data[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> j * N + i
        # Column-major: for fixed j, data[0..N-1, j] are contiguous in memory.
        # This makes all inner loops over i/k access data contiguously.

    # Symmetric covariance matrix: M x M.
    cov[p, q]: out DATA_TYPE = (p, q) -> p * M + q
        # Row-major: row p is contiguous. Access is still cache-friendly
        # when iterating over q for fixed p, and symmetry is explicitly exploited.

    # Column means (intermediate). Not needed after cov is produced, but kept
    # for clarity and to mirror the original code.
    mean[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j

parameters:
    # Number of observations as a scalar (matches original float_n).
    float_n: DATA_TYPE

    # Precomputed reciprocals to replace inner-loop divisions by multiplies.
    inv_float_n: DATA_TYPE           # = 1.0 / float_n
    inv_float_n_minus1: DATA_TYPE    # = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)

    # Tunable integer parameters for blocking / vectorization on the target CPU.
    TM: int                          # tile size for feature (M) dimension (e.g., 32 or 64)
    TN: int                          # tile size for observation (N) dimension (e.g., 256)
    VEC: int                         # vector width (e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles, 16 for AVX-512 floats)
    UNROLL_K: int                    # unroll factor for reductions over k (e.g., 4 or 8)

computation:
    # Precompute scale factors once (hoisted out of all loops).
    INV_N:
        inv_float_n = 1.0 / float_n
    INV_NM1:
        inv_float_n_minus1 = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)

    # 1) Compute column means:
    #
    #     mean[j] = (1 / float_n) * sum_{i=0..N-1} data[i, j]
    #
    # Implemented as a reduction over i for each column j.
    for j:
        MEAN[j]:
            mean[j] = inv_float_n * sum(k, data[k, j])
            # sum(k, ...) is implemented as a scalar accumulator in a register,
            # initialized to 0 and updated for k = 0..N-1.

    # 2) Center the data in-place by subtracting the column means:
    #
    #     data[i, j] ← data[i, j] - mean[j]
    #
    # After this step, each column has mean approximately zero.
    for j:
        for i:
            CENTER[i, j]:
                data[i, j] = data[i, j] - mean[j]

    # 3) Compute the covariance matrix:
    #
    #     cov[p, q] = (1 / (float_n - 1)) *
    #                  sum_{k=0..N-1} data[k, p] * data[k, q]
    #
    # on centered data, and then exploit symmetry: cov[q, p] = cov[p, q].
    # Only the upper triangle p <= q performs the expensive reduction.
    for p:
        for q:
            if p <= q:
                COV_UPPER[p, q]:
                    cov[p, q] = inv_float_n_minus1 *
                                 sum(k, data[k, p] * data[k, q])
                    # Again, sum(k, ...) is a local scalar accumulator
                    # to minimize repeated memory traffic for cov[p, q].
            else:
                COV_LOWER[p, q]:
                    cov[p, q] = cov[q, p]

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # Arithmetic & scalar hoisting
    # -----------------------------
    # - Replace the original per-element divisions by float_n and (float_n - 1.0)
    #   with single precomputed reciprocals inv_float_n, inv_float_n_minus1.
    # - INV_N and INV_NM1 are already written outside any data-dependent loops.
    hoist(INV_N)
    hoist(INV_NM1)

    # -----------------------------------
    # Data layout & access pattern choice
    # -----------------------------------
    # - Using column-major layout for data aligns with the kernel’s dominant access
    #   pattern: inner loops over the observation dimension (i/k) for fixed column(s)
    #   j, p, q. This yields contiguous memory accesses and maximizes vectorization.
    # - No extra full-size buffers are introduced; memory usage stays within
    #   the original footprint plus negligible scalars.

    # -------------------------------------
    # Mean and centering: per-column passes
    # -------------------------------------
    # Loops for MEAN and CENTER are:
    #   for j: for i: ...
    # With column-major data, the inner dimension (i) is contiguous.
    # Exploit parallelism across columns and vectorization across observations.

    parallelize(j)
        # Each column j is independent in MEAN and CENTER, so j can be
        # safely distributed across threads without reductions or races.

    vectorize(k, VEC)
        # Vectorize the reduction over k in MEAN[j] since data[k, j] is
        # contiguous in k for fixed j.

    vectorize(i, VEC)
        # Vectorize CENTER over i (contiguous in data[i, j]) to emit wide
        # loads/stores and a vector subtract.

    # Optionally unroll the inner reductions to hide latency further.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # ----------------------------------------------------
    # Covariance: blocked symmetric rank-k–style structure
    # ----------------------------------------------------
    # Treat covariance computation as a blocked symmetric rank-k update:
    #   C := C + A^T A, with A = centered data (N x M), C = cov (M x M).
    # Only the upper triangle is explicitly accumulated; the lower triangle
    # is filled via symmetry in COV_LOWER.

    # Tile feature dimensions (p, q) so a cov tile and the corresponding
    # data columns stay in cache, and tile the reduction dimension (k)
    # to improve reuse of data[k, *] within each tile.
    block(p, P, TM)   # P: outer tile index over rows of cov
    block(q, Q, TM)   # Q: outer tile index over columns of cov
    block(k, K, TN)   # K: outer tile index over observations (reduction dim)

    # Hoist the tile loops to the outside, giving the structure:
    #   for P, Q, K (outer tiles) { for p, q, k (intra-tile) { ... } }
    hoist(P)
    hoist(Q)
    hoist(K)

    # Parallelism:
    # - Each (P,Q) covariance tile is independent once data is centered.
    # - Within a tile, each p (row in the upper triangle) can be assigned
    #   to a thread without write conflicts:
    #     * COV_UPPER[p, q] computes cov[p, q] and cov[q, p] for q ≥ p.
    #     * No other p' loop writes cov[q, p] because the inner loop
    #       only visits q ≥ p.
    parallelize(P)
        # Distribute blocks of covariance rows across cores.

    # Vectorization:
    # - The inner reduction over K (k within a tile) touches contiguous
    #   data[K, p] and data[K, q] for fixed (p, q), ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(K, VEC)
    unroll(K, UNROLL_K)

    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Symmetry exploitation and lower-triangular fill stage
    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # COV_UPPER computes only entries with p <= q (upper triangle).
    # COV_LOWER copies the corresponding symmetric entries.
    # To make this explicit and movable:
    #
    # - Ensure all COV_UPPER(p, q) are computed before COV_LOWER uses them.
    # - COV_LOWER can then be run as a separate, highly parallelizable pass
    #   over (p, q) with p > q and simple scalar loads/stores.
    #
    # We express this as a hoisting of the symmetry-copy phase:
    hoist(COV_LOWER)
    parallelize(q)
        # The symmetry copy is pure, with no data dependencies between
        # different (p, q) pairs, so it can be fully parallelized.
--- END OF MODEL: covariance-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: covariance-04 ---
domain:
    # Problem sizes (taken from N, M in the C code)
    n: dim in [0, N)          # sample index, corresponds to loop variable i over N
    f: dim in [0, M)          # feature index, corresponds to loop variable j over M
    g: dim in [0, M)          # second feature index, for covariance pairs (i,j) over M

data:
    # Original data matrix: data[N][M], row-major in C (data[i][j] = i*M + j)
    data[n, f]: inout DATA_TYPE = (n, f) -> n * M + f

    # Mean vector: mean[M], 1D contiguous
    mean[f]: out DATA_TYPE    = (f) -> f

    # Covariance matrix: cov[M][M], row-major in C (cov[i][j] = i*M + j)
    cov[f, g]: out DATA_TYPE  = (f, g) -> f * M + g

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE                         # equals (DATA_TYPE)n in the C code

    # Arithmetic-strength reduction:
    # precompute reciprocals once instead of dividing inside large loops
    inv_float_n: DATA_TYPE                     # = 1.0 / float_n
    inv_float_n_minus_1: DATA_TYPE             # = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)

    # Tunable blocking / vectorization parameters (chosen for target machine)
    TN: int                                    # tile size along n (samples) for covariance, e.g., 128
    TM: int                                    # tile size along f,g (features), e.g., 32
    VEC_WIDTH: int                             # SIMD width in features, e.g., 4 or 8 depending on DATA_TYPE

computation:
    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 1: compute column means: mean[f] = (1/N) * sum_n data[n,f]
    # -----------------------------------------------------------

    MEAN_INIT:
        for f:
            mean[f] = 0.0

    # Accumulate in row-major order: iterate over samples n in outer position,
    # features f in inner position. This preserves the mathematical sum
    # mean[f] = sum_n data[n,f], but improves cache locality vs. the original
    # column-wise traversal.
    MEAN_ACCUM:
        for n, f:
            mean[f] += data[n, f]

    MEAN_SCALE:
        for f:
            mean[f] *= inv_float_n
            # Equivalent to mean[f] /= float_n in the C code.

    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 2: center data in-place: data[n,f] -= mean[f]
    # -----------------------------------------------------------

    CENTER:
        for n, f:
            data[n, f] = data[n, f] - mean[f]

    # At this point, data[n,f] holds the mean-centered data used for covariance.

    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 3: covariance of centered data
    #
    # cov[f,g] = 1/(float_n - 1) * sum_n data[n,f] * data[n,g]
    # Only the upper triangle (g >= f) is computed, and the lower
    # triangle is filled by symmetry, exactly as in the C code.
    # -----------------------------------------------------------

    # Initialize upper triangle of cov to zero
    COV_INIT:
        for f, g where g >= f:
            cov[f, g] = 0.0

    # Accumulate unscaled covariance in upper triangle.
    # Mathematically: cov[f,g] = sum_n data[n,f]*data[n,g]
    COV_ACCUM:
        for n, f, g where g >= f:
            cov[f, g] += data[n, f] * data[n, g]

    # Scale upper triangle by 1/(N-1)
    COV_SCALE:
        for f, g where g >= f:
            cov[f, g] *= inv_float_n_minus_1

    # Symmetrize: copy upper triangle into lower triangle.
    # For f == g (diagonal) this is a benign self-copy; for f < g
    # it enforces cov[g,f] = cov[f,g] as in the original kernel.
    COV_SYMM:
        for f, g where g > f:
            cov[g, f] = cov[f, g]

dependencies:
    # Means must be fully computed before centering, since CENTER uses mean[f].
    for f in [0, M):
        MEAN_SCALE(f) -> CENTER(*, f)

    # Centering must finish before covariance accumulation, since COV_ACCUM
    # operates on centered data.
    for n in [0, N), f in [0, M):
        CENTER(n, f) -> COV_INIT(*, *)        # initialization must be done before any accumulation
        CENTER(n, f) -> COV_ACCUM(*, *, *)    # and all centering must logically precede covariance

    # Covariance accumulation must complete before scaling, and scaling before symmetrization.
    for f in [0, M), g in [f, M):
        COV_INIT(f, g)   -> COV_ACCUM(*, f, g)
        COV_ACCUM(*, f, g) -> COV_SCALE(f, g)
        COV_SCALE(f, g)  -> COV_SYMM(f, *)    # each upper element used to fill lower triangle

optimization:
    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Scalar hoisting
    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Compute the reciprocals once outside the main loops.
    # This replaces many divisions by a pair of scalar divisions + many multiplies.
    hoist(inv_float_n)
    hoist(inv_float_n_minus_1)

    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 1: mean computation
    # -----------------------------------------------------------

    # MEAN_ACCUM is expressed as for n, f: mean[f] += data[n,f].
    # We optimize it to:
    #   - stream data row-major (n outer, f inner),
    #   - vectorize across f,
    #   - parallelize over n with a reduction into mean[f].
    MEAN_ACCUM:
        # Row-major streaming is already captured by the (n, f) loop order
        # used in computation; no further interchange needed.

        vectorize(f, VEC_WIDTH)
        # Use SIMD to accumulate multiple features' partial sums per iteration.

        parallelize(n)
        # Parallelization over n uses a reduction on mean[f]:
        #   - Each thread holds a private mean_local[f],
        #   - accumulates its subset of rows,
        #   - and then mean[f] is formed by summing mean_local[f] over threads.
        # This adds O(M * num_threads) temporary storage, which remains well
        # below the +50% memory budget relative to the original data+cov+mean.

    MEAN_INIT:
        vectorize(f, VEC_WIDTH)

    MEAN_SCALE:
        vectorize(f, VEC_WIDTH)
        parallelize(f)
        # Scaling of mean[f] is embarrassingly parallel.

    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 2: centering
    # -----------------------------------------------------------

    CENTER:
        # Traverse data in row-major order: n outer, f inner, as written.
        vectorize(f, VEC_WIDTH)
        # Subtract mean[f] from multiple contiguous elements in a row at once.

        parallelize(n)
        # Each row n is independent once mean is known.
        # Threads share read-only mean[f] and write disjoint slices data[n,*].

    # -----------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase 3: covariance
    # -----------------------------------------------------------

    # We treat COV_ACCUM as a symmetric rank-k update:
    #   cov = cov + sum_n (x_n^T x_n), where x_n is the n-th centered row.
    # To improve cache locality for cov and data simultaneously:
    #   - Block the feature dimensions (f,g) so each cov tile fits in cache.
    #   - Optionally block n to balance between reusing cov tiles and
    #     streaming data rows.
    #
    # Triangular constraint (g >= f) is preserved by skipping tiles
    # strictly below the diagonal or by clipping their internal (f,g) loops.

    COV_ACCUM:
        # 3D blocking
        block(f, F, TM)        # F indexes tiles along feature-row dimension
        block(g, G, TM)        # G indexes tiles along feature-col dimension
        block(n, N_blk, TN)    # N_blk indexes tiles along samples

        hoist(F)
        hoist(G)
        hoist(N_blk)
        # Outer structure after blocking (conceptually):
        #   for F in seq(0, ceil(M/TM)):
        #     for G in seq(F, ceil(M/TM)):          # enforce upper tiles only
        #       for N_blk in seq(0, ceil(N/TN)):
        #         for n in tile N_blk:
        #           for f in tile F:
        #             for g in tile G with g >= f:
        #               cov[f,g] += data[n,f] * data[n,g]

        # Within each (F,G,N_blk) tile:
        vectorize(g, VEC_WIDTH)
        # Vectorize across contiguous g for a fixed (n,f).
        # This turns the inner g-loop into efficient SIMD FMAs.

        parallelize(F)
        # Parallelize over feature-row tiles F:
        #   - Each thread owns a disjoint band of cov rows (a set of tiles (F,*)).
        #   - Within each band, tiles (F,G) for G >= F are independent of tiles
        #     handled by other threads (no write-write conflicts).
        #   - All threads read shared centered data[n,f] rows.

    COV_INIT:
        block(f, F, TM)
        block(g, G, TM)
        hoist(F)
        hoist(G)
        vectorize(g, VEC_WIDTH)
        parallelize(F)
        # Initialize upper-triangular tiles of cov in parallel.

    COV_SCALE:
        block(f, F, TM)
        block(g, G, TM)
        hoist(F)
        hoist(G)
        vectorize(g, VEC_WIDTH)
        parallelize(F)
        # Scale each upper-triangular tile cov[f,g] by inv_float_n_minus_1.
        # No dependencies between elements within the upper triangle.

    COV_SYMM:
        block(f, F, TM)
        block(g, G, TM)
        hoist(F)
        hoist(G)
        vectorize(g, VEC_WIDTH)
        parallelize(F)
        # For each upper-triangular element cov[f,g] (g > f) in a tile,
        # copy it to the symmetric position cov[g,f]. Each pair (f,g) is
        # written exactly once, and threads operate on disjoint (f,*) bands.

# Notes:
# - All transformations preserve the mathematical definitions:
#     mean[f] = (1/N) * sum_n data[n,f] (before centering),
#     data is mean-centered,
#     cov[f,g] = 1/(N-1) * sum_n data_centered[n,f] * data_centered[n,g],
#   and cov is explicitly symmetrized (cov[g,f] = cov[f,g]).
#
# - The only semantic difference vs. the original C is the reassociation
#   of floating-point additions due to loop reordering and blocking.
#   This is consistent with the reduction-based formulation used here.
--- END OF MODEL: covariance-04 ---

domain:
    n: dim in [0, N)         # sample index (rows of `data`)
    m: dim in [0, M)         # feature index / column
    p: dim in [0, M)         # second feature index (for covariance pairs)

data:
    # All arrays are stored row-major in memory.
    data[n, m]: inout DATA_TYPE = (n, m) -> n * M + m    # N×M input, then mean-centered in place
    cov[m, p]: out   DATA_TYPE = (m, p) -> m * M + p     # M×M covariance matrix
    mean[m]:  inout DATA_TYPE = (m)    -> m              # length-M vector of column means

parameters:
    float_n: DATA_TYPE              # == (DATA_TYPE) N in the original code
    inv_float_n: DATA_TYPE          # 1.0 / float_n        (precomputed)
    inv_float_n_minus1: DATA_TYPE   # 1.0 / (float_n - 1.) (precomputed)

    # Tuning parameters:
    TM: int   # tile size along feature dimensions (i,j), e.g., 32 or 64
    TN: int   # tile size along sample dimension n, e.g., 64
    VF_mean: int  # SIMD width used when vectorizing over m (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double)
    VF_cov:  int  # SIMD width for covariance updates over p

computation:
    # Replace per-element divisions with two scalar reciprocals.
    inv_float_n         = 1.0 / float_n
    inv_float_n_minus1  = 1.0 / (float_n - 1.0)

    # 1. Column means:
    #    mean[j] = (1/float_n) * sum_{n=0..N-1} data[n, j]
    for m in [0, M):
        mean[m] = inv_float_n * sum(n in [0, N), data[n, m])

    # 2. Mean-centering:
    #    data[n, m] <- data[n, m] - mean[m]
    for n in [0, N), m in [0, M):
        data[n, m] = data[n, m] - mean[m]

    # 3. Covariance on centered data:
    #    For 0 <= i <= j < M:
    #       cov[i, j] = (1/(float_n - 1)) * sum_{n} data[n, i] * data[n, j]
    #       cov[j, i] = cov[i, j]
    for m in [0, M):
        for p in [m, M):
            cov[m, p] = inv_float_n_minus1 * sum(n in [0, N),
                                                 data[n, m] * data[n, p])
            cov[p, m] = cov[m, p]

dependencies:
    # Means must be computed before centering.
    for m in [0, M):
        mean[m] -> for n in [0, N): data[n, m]

    # Centering must complete before covariance accumulation.
    for n in [0, N), m in [0, M):
        data[n, m] -> for i in [0, M), p in [i, M): cov[i, p]

optimization:
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Scalar strength reduction
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Compute inv_float_n and inv_float_n_minus1 once, and use
    # multiplications instead of divides inside the loops.
    hoist(inv_float_n)
    hoist(inv_float_n_minus1)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Mean computation: row-major traversal + reduction
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mathematical definition (order-free) is:
    #   mean[m] = inv_float_n * sum_n data[n,m]
    #
    # Reorder the accumulation loops to traverse `data` row-major,
    # improving cache use and SIMD efficiency.
    #
    # Conceptually transform:
    #   for m in [0,M):
    #       mean[m] = 0
    #       for n in [0,N):
    #           mean[m] += data[n,m]
    #
    # into:
    #   for m in [0,M): mean[m] = 0
    #   for n in [0,N):
    #       for m in [0,M):
    #           mean[m] += data[n,m]
    #
    # which is equivalent but uses contiguous accesses along m.
    interchange(n, m)        # in the loop computing the sum for mean

    # Initialize `mean[m]` once outside the main accumulation loop.
    hoist(m)                 # hoist mean[m] = 0.0 to the outermost possible level

    # Vectorize across the contiguous feature dimension.
    vectorize(m, VF_mean)

    # Parallelize over rows `n` when computing means.
    # This implies a reduction on mean[m], typically implemented with
    # per-thread private mean[m] arrays and a final merge; memory
    # overhead remains well below +50% of the original footprint.
    parallelize(n)           # with reduction over mean[m]

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Mean-centering: straightforward SIMD + threading
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Centering loop already uses row-major traversal (n outer, m inner).
    # Expose its data parallelism:
    vectorize(m, VF_mean)
    parallelize(n)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Covariance computation: outer-product form + tiling
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Mathematically we have:
    #   cov[i,j] = inv_float_n_minus1 * sum_n data[n,i] * data[n,j], i<=j
    #
    # The original kernel uses loop order (i, j, n), which rescans the
    # rows of `data` for every (i,j) pair. Instead, we reuse each row
    # as a vector x_n and perform rank-1 outer-product updates:
    #
    #   For each n:
    #     cov += x_n^T * x_n
    #
    # Equivalent loop structure:
    #   for n in [0,N):
    #     for i in [0,M):
    #       xi = data[n,i]
    #       for j in [i,M):
    #         cov[i,j] += xi * data[n,j]
    #
    # which preserves the same sum but reuses the row x_n from L1.
    #
    # Express this as a loop transformation from (i,j,n) to (n,i,j):
    interchange(n, m)        # move sample loop `n` outside (m,p) in the covariance region
    hoist(n)                 # make `n` the outermost loop for covariance

    # Now tile the feature-space loops so that sub-blocks of `cov`
    # live in L1/L2 during updates. TM is tuned to cache size.
    block(m, M_blk, TM)      # tiles for cov row index (i)
    block(p, P_blk, TM)      # tiles for cov column index (j)

    # Only process upper-triangular tiles (P_blk >= M_blk); within
    # each tile, guard with `if (p >= m)` as needed to preserve
    # the i<=j constraint. This does not change the numerical result.

    # Optionally tile the sample dimension for very large N to balance
    # reuse of `data` and `cov`:
    block(n, N_blk, TN)

    # Within a (M_blk, P_blk, N_blk) tile, vectorize across contiguous
    # columns p when performing:
    #   cov[m,p] += data[n,m] * data[n,p]
    vectorize(P_blk, VF_cov)

    # Parallelize across independent tiles of cov’s upper triangle.
    # Each (M_blk, P_blk) tile owns a disjoint sub-block of `cov`,
    # so threads do not need synchronization during accumulation.
    parallelize(M_blk)

    # Final scaling and symmetric fill:
    #   cov[i,j] *= inv_float_n_minus1; cov[j,i] = cov[i,j]
    # is itself trivially vectorizable and parallelizable.
    vectorize(p, VF_cov)
    parallelize(m)

/* covariance.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "covariance.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int m, int n,
		 DATA_TYPE *float_n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m))
{
  int i, j;

  *float_n = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < M; j++)
      data[i][j] = ((DATA_TYPE) i*j) / M;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int m,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(cov,M,M,m,m))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("cov");
  for (i = 0; i < m; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < m; j++) {
      if ((i * m + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
      fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, cov[i][j]);
    }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("cov");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_covariance[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int m, int n,
		       DATA_TYPE float_n,
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(data,N,M,n,m),
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(cov,M,M,m,m),
		       DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(mean,M,m))
{
  int i, j, k;

#pragma scop
  for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
    {
      mean[j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
      for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
        mean[j] += data[i][j];
      mean[j] /= float_n;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < _PB_M; j++)
      data[i][j] -= mean[j];

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_M; i++)
    for (j = i; j < _PB_M; j++)
      {
        cov[i][j] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
        for (k = 0; k < _PB_N; k++)
	  cov[i][j] += data[k][i] * data[k][j];
        cov[i][j] /= (float_n - SCALAR_VAL(1.0));
        cov[j][i] = cov[i][j];
      }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;
  int m = M;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  DATA_TYPE float_n;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(data,DATA_TYPE,N,M,n,m);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(cov,DATA_TYPE,M,M,m,m);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(mean,DATA_TYPE,M,m);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (m, n, &float_n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_covariance (m, n, float_n,
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(data),
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(cov),
		     POLYBENCH_ARRAY(mean));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(m, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(cov)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(data);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(cov);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(mean);

  return 0;
}
